<p align="center"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">PART I</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="item1business"></a><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Item 1. Business</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="general"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">General</font></u></b></p>

<p><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. (&ldquo;Holdings&rdquo;), a Delaware corporation, was incorporated in August 1996 and is engaged in the business of
transporting people.&nbsp; Our principal asset is all of the issued and outstanding shares of stock of XJT Holdings, Inc., the sole stockholder of ExpressJet Airlines, Inc. (referred to in this report as &ldquo;Airlines&rdquo; and, together with XJT Holdings, Inc.
and Holdings, as &ldquo;ExpressJet&rdquo;, &ldquo;Company&rdquo;, &ldquo;we&rdquo; or &ldquo;us&rdquo;).&nbsp; Airlines currently operates a fleet of 244 aircraft flying under contractual arrangements for network carriers and entities desiring cost-effective and
fully customizable group travel.&nbsp; Airlines is one of the largest regional airlines in the world based on 2009 available seat miles, fleet size and passengers transported.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, ExpressJet continued to transition its business by focusing on contractual flying arrangements.&nbsp; <font color="black">In addition, we placed emphasis on
improving our balance</font> sheet in light of the pressures of industry-wide capacity reductions and continued difficulties in the global economy.&nbsp; These efforts included the repurchase of $8.7 million of our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 in the
open market, which reduced the outstanding principal balance of our convertible notes from $60.8 million as of December 31, 2008 to $52.1 million as of December 31, 2009.&nbsp; We also repurchased 3.0 million shares of our common stock in 2009.&nbsp; In late 2009, we
began to reallocate aircraft within our fleet to immediately support existing capacity needs of United under the United Express Agreement.&nbsp; Additionally, revenues increased over 40% in 2009 within our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="2" face="Arial"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">For substantially all of 2009, we operated 214 aircraft for Continental as Continental Express under the Amended Continental CPA and 30 aircraft
within our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.&nbsp; In early 2010, we executed the United Express Agreement, which has a retroactive effective date of December 1, 2009, pursuant to which we will operate 22 ERJ-145 aircraft as United Express to replace flying
performed by other United Express partner carriers whose contracts have expired.&nbsp; We operated a total of six aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of December 31, 2009 and a total of 16 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of February 15,
2010.&nbsp; The remaining six aircraft will begin operating under the United Express Agreement on March 1, 2010.&nbsp; On February 15, 2010, we entered into the First Amendment to the United Express Agreement with United, pursuant to which we will fly up to ten
additional aircraft for United in the current ExpressJet livery from May 2010 through December 2010.&nbsp; With the addition of this flying, we expect our 2010 fleet of 244 aircraft to be allocated as follows:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="672">
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">206 aircraft operating for Continental as Continental Express pursuant to the Amended Continental CPA;</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">22 aircraft operating for United as United Express pursuant to the United Express Agreement, with an additional ten aircraft operating as United Express from May 2010 to December 2010 pursuant to the First Amendment to the United
Express Agreement; and</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">16 aircraft operating in our Corporate Aviation (charter) division, decreasing to as few as six aircraft from May 2010 to December 2010.</font></p>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <font color="black">We also provide aviation services through our two wholly owned subsidiaries, ExpressJet Services, LLC and InTech Aerospace Services, LP
(&ldquo;InTech&rdquo;) and through our and majority owned subsidiary, Saltillo Jet Center, S. de R.L. C.V. (&ldquo;Saltillo&rdquo;).&nbsp; These services include ground-handling at airport locations across the United States, aircraft composite repair and overhaul,
and aircraft interior refurbishments (interiors and paint).&nbsp; During the first half of 2007, we rebranded InTech and Saltillo so that each does business under the &ldquo;ExpressJet Services&rdquo; trade name.&nbsp; These entities are collectively referred to
herein as &ldquo;ExpressJet Services&rdquo;.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We compete with a number of regional airlines for the service we provide to our main-line airline partners and charter customers.&nbsp; We believe that our continued
success depends on our ability to provide our partners and charter customers outstanding operational performance and customer service at a competitive price.&nbsp; Our ability to do this depends on the commitment of and execution by our over 5,600 employees on a
daily basis.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="ourbusinesssegments"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Our Business Segments</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u>2009 Business Segments</u></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For the year ended December 31, 2009, <font color="black">ExpressJet had two reportable segments which are the basis of our internal financial reporting: Contract Flying
and Aviation Services.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Contract Flying includes flying conducted in our Corporate Aviation (charter) division under the Amended Continental CPA and under the United Express
Agreement.&nbsp; Under Contract Flying, revenues are contractually determined, eliminating our exposure to fluctuations in yields and passenger volumes.&nbsp; Under these arrangements, our partners also bear the risk and cost of fuel, aircraft ownership, airport
services, and marketing and distribution.&nbsp; We are responsible for the operation and maintenance of the aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> Aviation Services includes components related to our ground-handling services and ExpressJet <font color="black">Services.&nbsp;</font> Under
ExpressJet Services&rsquo; brand, we paint aircraft and repair composite structures, aircraft interiors (including refurbishment of seats, galleys, lavatories and panels) and thrust reversers throughout our four facilities in the United States and Mexico.&nbsp; In
the first quarter of 2009, we sold substantially all of the assets of <font color="black">American Composites, LLC (&ldquo;American Composites&rdquo;), a wholly owned subsidiary previously part of ExpressJet Services.&nbsp; Additionally, we sold an approximately
74,000 square foot building in Miami, Florida that was owned by XJT Florida, Inc. (&ldquo;XJT Florida&rdquo;) and leased to American Composites for use as a maintenance/composites shop.</font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>Business Segments prior to 2009</u></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Prior to 2009, <font color="black">ExpressJet had three reportable segments: Branded Flying, Contract Flying, and Aviation Services.&nbsp; Branded Flying, which began in
2007, included operations under the ExpressJet brand and a pro-rate flying arrangement (the &ldquo;Delta Prorate&rdquo;) under the Delta Airlines, Inc. (&ldquo;Delta&rdquo;) brand.&nbsp; Revenues for this flying were derived from passengers flying on scheduled air
service.&nbsp; We were responsible for local market pricing, scheduling and revenue management, and the operation and maintenance of the aircraft.&nbsp; Our flying under the Delta Prorate provided us with a prorated portion of the airfare plus an incentive for
passengers connecting onto Delta's network.&nbsp; In September 2008, we suspended Branded Flying in response to high fuel costs and other challenges facing the airline industry at such time.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <font color="black">Contract Flying prior to 2009 included our Corporate Aviation (charter) division and our capacity purchase agreements with Continental and
Delta.</font></font></p>

<p><a name="productsservices"></a><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></u></p>

<p><b><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">Our Products and Services</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, we continued to build on our ability to provide unique group travel experiences through our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.&nbsp; In addition, we
expanded our contractual flying for other mainline air carriers through the United Express Agreement.&nbsp; Prior to 2007, virtually all of our revenue came from our original capacity purchase agreement with Continental (the &ldquo;Original Continental CPA&rdquo;)
supported by a fleet of 274 aircraft.&nbsp; In recent years, our revenue streams have diversified to include our new partner, United, and a multitude of charter clients.&nbsp; These new customers benefit from our offering of cost effective and reliable travel
solutions.&nbsp; Key to our product offering is an infrastructure base that allows us to leverage the economies and reliability of a fleet comprised on only one type of aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; This infrastructure is important to our success and supports:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u>Contract Flying</u></b></font></p>

<p><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we averaged more than 1,045 daily Contract Flying flights, offering scheduled passenger service to over 134 scheduled destinations in North
America, including Mexico, and also the Caribbean.&nbsp; We generated $654.2 million of revenue, over 95% of our total consolidated revenue, in this segment during 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="cappurch"></a><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Continental Capacity Purchase and Other Agreements</i></font></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></b> A significant portion of our revenue and cash flows is attributable to the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA,
Airlines operates flights on behalf of Continental as Continental Express.&nbsp; Continental controls and is responsible for scheduling; pricing and managing seat inventories and is entitled to all revenue associated with the operation of the aircraft.&nbsp; We also
have various other agreements with Continental that govern our relationship.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, we are not exposed to certain costs normally associated with operating an airline, as all reservations, sales, marketing and
distribution, aircraft ownership and fuel costs are borne entirely by Continental.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="2" face="Arial"></font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><u><font size="2">2008 Amended Continental CPA</font></u></i></b><font size="2">.&nbsp; In June 2008, we reached an agreement with Continental to amend the
Original Continental CPA.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA, which became effective July 1, 2008, has a seven-year term that is scheduled to expire on June 30, 2015.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental compensates us at a pre-determined rate based on
block hours flown and reimburses us for various pass-through expenses including passenger liability insurance, hull insurance, war risk insurance, landing fees and substantially all regional jet engine expenses under current long-term third-party contracts with no
margin or mark-up.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel and paying aircraft rent for all flights operated as Continental Express; therefore, these items are not included in our Consolidated
Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; The fixed block hour rates are considerably lower than the rates under the original agreement, though they are also subject to annual escalations tied to a consumer price index (capped at 3.5%) at
each anniversary date, July 1.&nbsp; The consumer price index escalation used for the July 1, 2009 rate adjustment was 1.94%.&nbsp; <font color="black">We will continue to focus on aggressively managing</font> costs as certain of our costs currently have contractual
escalations that are higher then the current index escalation under the Amended Continental CPA, and the economic difficulties facing the entire airline industry.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">Concurrently with the execution of the Amended Continental CPA, we entered into a settlement agreement with Continental to release the
parties&rsquo; claims relating to certain identified payments under the Original Continental CPA, including disputes previously disclosed as possible matters for arbitration.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">In September 2008, we agreed with Continental on the first amendment to the Amended Continental CPA in order to compensate us for our fixed costs
considered in the calculation of the pre-determined block hour rates, which cannot be reduced as a result of the unanticipated reduction in aircraft utilization by Continental&rsquo;s scheduling. We also agreed that if Continental, beginning in year two, increases
its aircraft utilization above a pre-determined threshold, then it may receive discounts on the agreed, pre-determined block hour rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In December 2008, we agreed with Continental on the second amendment to the Amended Continental CPA in order to clarify certain issues related to our revenue
recognition, the fuel efficiency program in place in connection with the Amended Continental CPA and depreciation related to the aircraft we operate for Continental and excess inventory related thereto.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">Pursuant to the terms of the first and second amendments to the Amended Continental CPA, beginning in July 2009 and
throughout the remainder of term of the Amended Continental CPA, <font color="black">if Continental increases utilization of our aircraft above a pre-determined threshold, then Continental will be entitled to receive a discount on the agreed, pre-determined block
hour rates; provided that the aggregate discount received by Continental shall not exceed $10 million throughout the remainder of the term.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In December 2009, we agreed with Continental on the third amendment to the Amended Continental CPA pursuant to which, among other things, we agreed to sublease eight
aircraft from Continental that were previously operated as Continental Express under the Amended Continental CPA in order to meet our aircraft requirements under the United Express Agreement.</font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>Scope of Agreement.</u></font></i></b>&nbsp; For substantially all of 2009, the Amended Continental CPA covered 214 of Airlines&rsquo; existing fleet of 244
aircraft.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA provides that we will fly a minimum <font color="black">of 190 aircraft for the remainder of the term.&nbsp; Currently, we are flying 206 aircraft as Continental Express under the Amended Continental CPA, which reflects the
removal of eight aircraft in late 2009 that we intend to use for flying under our United Express Agreement as well as our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.</font> Continental does not have the ability to terminate the agreement without cause prior to the
termination date and cannot reduce the number of aircraft covered under the agreement below 190 aircraft.&nbsp; However, the Amended Continental CPA may cover less than 190 aircraft if there is an expiration of a Covered Aircraft head lease and there are no
fifty-seat replacement aircraft (among the original 274 aircraft) being stored on behalf of Continental. &nbsp; If, at any time prior to the end of the Amended Continental CPA term, Continental proposes to engage any third party to operate one of the original 274
aircraft for Continental, we will have the right of first opportunity to operate that aircraft.&nbsp;</p>

Amended Continental CPA states that:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; So long as scheduled flights under the Amended Continental CPA represent at least 50% of all our scheduled flights, or at least 200 of our aircraft are operated as
Continental Express under the agreement, we are required to allocate our crews, maintenance personnel, facilities and other resources on a priority basis to scheduled flights under the agreement above all of our other flights and aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b> <b><i><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Aircraft Financing.</font></u></i></b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp; Airlines currently leases or
subleases all of its existing aircraft from Continental.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is required to purchase or lease from Embraer or its designee aircraft operated under the agreement, participate in the financing and to lease or sublease
these aircraft to us.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for paying the aircraft rent for all flights operating as Continental Express; therefore, these items are not included in our Consolidated Statements of Operations for
periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Aircraft withdrawn from the Amended Continental CPA become &ldquo;Uncovered Aircraft&rdquo; as defined in the agreement.&nbsp; Lease payments relating to uncovered aircraft, including the eight aircraft subleased from
Continental in late 2009, are at reduced rental rates, and rental payments for each such aircraft are fixed upon lease execution with no escalation clauses.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During 2009, our remaining 50 options with Embraer for aircraft purchases within the Embraer ERJ-145XR, ERJ-145LR AND ERJ-145ER aircraft (the &ldquo;ERJ-145
Family&rdquo;) expired unexercised.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We do not have the right to retain any aircraft removed from the Amended Continental CPA for use in our other operations if (i) they are removed by Continental as the
result of its termination of the agreement for cause, (ii) we have already retained 150 aircraft, including the 38 being subleased at reduced rent, or (iii) they are among aircraft owned by Continental, currently 18 aircraft.&nbsp; In all other events, we can elect
to retain any of the aircraft withdrawn from the Amended Continental CPA, most likely upon termination of the agreement, either at the end of seven years or upon early termination of the aircraft lease.&nbsp; In certain circumstances, in order to retain the aircraft
we will have to provide Continental with a full release from the head lease for such aircraft.&nbsp; Depending on the type of termination, there are procedures for notice and time for us to elect how many aircraft we will retain (with Continental selecting the
individual aircraft and engines), wind-down schedules of differing lengths, and maintenance reimbursements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i><u>Airport Facilities, Slots and Route Authorities</u></i><u>.</u></font></b>&nbsp; Most of the airport facilities that Airlines uses in its Continental Express
operation are leased from airport authorities by Continental.&nbsp; Under Airlines&rsquo; master facility and ground handling agreement with Continental, Airlines is entitled to use these facilities to fulfill its obligations under the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp;
However, it is not permitted to use airport terminal facilities leased by Continental to service other carriers or operate flights under its own code without Continental&rsquo;s approval.&nbsp; Furthermore, we must use those facilities that are non-terminal
facilities on a priority basis to support the scheduled flights that Airlines flies on behalf of Continental so long as those flights constitute at least 50% of our total scheduled flights or at least 200 of our aircraft are operated as Continental Express under the
Amended Continental CPA.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Ground Handling.</u>&nbsp;</i></b> During 2008, Continental began transitioning our ground handling services at all of their airport locations to an all
Continental managed program, with us providing specific ground handling services at a majority of these stations under an industry-standard ground handling agreement at fixed rates, outside of the Amended Continental CPA. This transition was completed in 2009.
Continental managed stations in which Continental has awarded us the ground handling contract are reflected in our Aviation Services line of business.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Prior to that time, Airlines provided ground handling and other support services, including baggage handling, station operations, ticketing, gate access and other
passenger, aircraft and traffic servicing functions for Continental at several of our airport locations under the Original Continental CPA.&nbsp; In exchange, Continental paid us an amount equal to Airlines&rsquo; incremental cost for providing those services.&nbsp;
Continental provided the same services for Airlines at its stations, including its hub airports.&nbsp; The cost for those services was based on the number of scheduled aircraft and the rates stipulated in the Original Continental CPA.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Labor Disruption.</u></i></b>&nbsp; Upon the occurrence of a union-authorized labor strike, the Amended Continental CPA provides that:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In addition, a labor disruption other than a union-authorized strike may cause us to be in material breach of the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; Under the agreement,
whenever Airlines fails to complete at least 90% of its aggregate scheduled flights (based on available seat miles) in three consecutive calendar months or at least 75% of its aggregate scheduled flights (based on available seat miles) in any 45-day period (in each
case, excluding flights cancelled due to union-authorized labor strikes, weather, air traffic control or non-carrier specific airworthiness directives or regulatory orders), we will be deemed to be in material breach of the agreement.&nbsp; In addition, if we have a
controllable completion factor for any two consecutive months of 97.5% or below, or a controllable on-time departure rate for any 60 consecutive days of 82.5% or below, we will be in material breach of the agreement.&nbsp; A labor disruption other than a
union-authorized strike could cause Airlines to fail to meet these operational requirements and, as a result, cause us to be in material breach of the agreement.&nbsp; See further discussions below regarding remedies for breach of the agreement by either Continental
or us.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Term and Termination of Agreement and Remedies for Breach</u></i><u>.</u></b>&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA is scheduled to terminate on June 30,
2015.&nbsp; Continental may terminate the agreement for cause without notice.&nbsp; &ldquo;Cause&rdquo; is defined as:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Continental may also terminate the agreement at any time upon our material breach that does not constitute cause, but continues uncured for 90&nbsp;days after we receive
notice of the breach.&nbsp; In addition, Continental may terminate the agreement immediately without notice or giving us an opportunity to cure if it makes a reasonable and good faith determination, using recognized standards of safety, that there is a material
safety concern with our operation of any flights under the Amended Continental CPA.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; If Continental materially breaches the agreement and fails to cure the breach within 60&nbsp;days after we notify it of the breach, we will be entitled to obtain our
payments directly from an airline clearing house from the 60th day for the duration of the default.&nbsp; In addition, Continental and we are each entitled to seek damages in arbitration and to reach equitable remedies.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i><u>Disposition of Aircraft upon Early Termination.</u></i></font></b>&nbsp; If Continental terminates the Amended Continental CPA for cause or breach, it will also
have the right at that time to terminate Airlines&rsquo; leases or subleases for aircraft operating as Continental Express under the agreement and take possession of these aircraft.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i><u>Amendment of Embraer and Rolls Royce Contracts.</u></i></font></b>&nbsp; We are prohibited, without Continental&rsquo;s consent, from amending Airlines&rsquo;
aircraft purchase agreements with Embraer for the original 274 aircraft to change the pricing, financing or leasing arrangements, or to make any other changes that may be expected to adversely affect Continental&rsquo;s rights under the Amended Continental CPA or our
ability to perform our obligations under the agreement.&nbsp; We have also agreed to acquire Continental&rsquo;s consent for any amendment of Airlines&rsquo; Embraer aircraft purchase agreements that reduce the financing or other obligations of Continental, provided
that the amendment does not increase Airlines&rsquo; obligations under these agreements.&nbsp; We are also prohibited, without Continental&rsquo;s consent, from amending our power-by-the-hour agreement with Rolls Royce Corporation (&ldquo;Rolls Royce&rdquo;) in any
manner that adversely affects Continental&rsquo;s or our engine maintenance costs for the aircraft subject to the Amended Continental CPA.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><u>Other Agreements with Continental.</u></i></b>&nbsp; Airlines has a fuel purchasing agreement with Continental, under which Continental is
directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel for all flights operating as Continental Express; therefore, fuel expense is not included in our Consolidated Statement of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Airlines also has an administrative
services agreement with Continental, under which Continental provides, at its expense, certain administrative support and information services in connection with the Amended Continental CPA.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In addition, we have a tax agreement with Continental that provides, among other things, for our payment of all or a significant portion of the tax benefits we realize
as a result of an internal reorganization performed before our initial public offering in 2002.&nbsp; Since our initial public offering, we have made net payments of approximately $122.5 million to Continental under the tax agreement and could make additional
payments to Continental through 2017.&nbsp; Payments to Continental would be conditional on our achieving taxable income and our ability to utilize the tax benefit described above.&nbsp; Refer to Note 8, &ldquo;Income Taxes,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated
Financial Statements</i> for further discussion of income taxes, including the tax agreement with Continental.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>United Express Agreement and Other Agreements</i></b></font></p>

<p><i><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></i></p>

<p><font size="3" color="black" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">General.</font></u></i></b><b><i><font size="2" color="black" face=
"Arial">&nbsp;</font></i></b> <font size="2" face="Arial">United announced in November 2009 that we were awarded a multiyear arrangement to fly 22 ERJ-145 aircraft as United Express.&nbsp; In February 2010, ExpressJet announced the execution of the United Express
Agreement, which agreement has an effective date retroactive to December 1, 2009.&nbsp; The United Express Agreement has an initial term expiring on April 30, 2012 for 11 aircraft and on April 30, 2013 for the remaining 11 aircraft, and contains a renewal option, at
United&rsquo;s election, for additional periods up to a total term of five years.&nbsp;&nbsp; Under this arrangement, United must notify ExpressJet of its intention to renew each group of aircraft <a name="_DV_C258">not less than</a> six month&rsquo;s prior to the
end of the term for such aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We operated a total of 6 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and a total of 16 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of
February 15, 1010.&nbsp; The remaining 6 aircraft will begin operating under the United Express Agreement on March 1, 2010.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="_DV_M218"></a><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On February 15, 2010, we entered into the First Amendment to the United Express Agreement with United, pursuant to which we will fly up to 10
additional for United in the current ExpressJet livery from May 2010 though December 2010.&nbsp; United will have the option to renew these supplemental aircraft for up to four additional periods of not less than thirty days per renewal period.&nbsp; Under this
arrangement, United must notify ExpressJet of its intention to renew for the initial renewal period no later than June 15, 2010 for the first six supplemental aircraft and August 15, 2010 for the remaining four additional aircraft.&nbsp; In an effort to provide
United with increased flexibility, the amendment allows United to extend the renewal deadline for each aircraft upon certain terms and conditions.&nbsp; If United elects not to extend the term of the supplemental aircraft, the ten aircraft will be removed from
service, and placed into the Corporate Aviation (charter) operation.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; All of the aircraft operated as United Express will be sourced from our Corporate Aviation (charter) division and leased as necessary from alternate sources.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the terms of the United Express Agreement, United will be responsible for scheduling, marketing, pricing and revenue management on the aircraft and collecting all
passenger revenues under the United brand.&nbsp; Airlines' operates, maintains and finances the aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We received payments under the United Express Agreement at a pre-determined rate based on block hours and departures flown and we are reimbursed us for various
pass-through expenses including passenger liability insurance, hull insurance, war risk insurance, landing fees and fuel.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The United Express Agreement also provides for incentives and penalties based upon Airlines&rsquo; performance, including on-time arrival performance and completion
percentage rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Warrant.</u></i>&nbsp;</b> As part of the United Express Agreement, on February 17, 2010, we issued a warrant to United for the purchase of 2.7 million shares
of common stock with an exercise price of $0.01 per share of common stock.&nbsp; We did not issue this warrant for any specified consideration, but instead in connection with The United Express Agreement covering 22 ERJ-145 aircraft for United Express service
effective December 1, 2009.&nbsp; The certificate representing the warrant contains (and certificates representing the underlying shares, when issued, will contain) restrictive legends preventing sale, transfer or other disposition, unless registered under the
Securities Act or pursuant to an exemption thereunder.&nbsp; The warrant shall terminate and become void as of the earlier of (a) the time and date the warrant is fully exercised with respect to all warrant shares pursuant to the warrant and (b) 5:00 p.m., central
time, on the date of the expiration (with respect to all tranches of aircraft and including renewal terms) or earlier termination of the United Express Agreement; provided that if the United Express Agreement is terminated due to any material default or breach by
ExpressJet, the warrant shall not terminate or become void and shall continue in full force and effect until April 30, 2013.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For additional information regarding the United Express Agreement, refer to Item 1A, <i>Risk Factors</i>.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Corporate Aviation</i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b> In late 2009, 30 aircraft were assigned/utilized within our corporate aviation (charter) division, and subject to long-term agreements and
other ad-hoc charter service arrangements.&nbsp; Our Corporate Aviation (charter) division continues to focus on corporate shuttles, entertainment / sports, and government businesses.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, our Corporate Aviation (charter) division had firm
contracts for over 50% of budgeted revenues for 2010.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Corporate Aviation&rsquo;s goal is to provide group travelers a comfortable, cost-effective and fully customizable travel experience that is unmatched by our
competitors.&nbsp; Our travel solutions are provided to corporations, collegiate and professional sports teams, government entities, hotel and gaming properties, hospitality companies, bands and other entities, including airlines.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The aircraft are flown under Airlines&rsquo; operating certificate issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (the &ldquo;FAA&rdquo;).</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u><font color="black">Fuel</font></u></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, the United Express Agreement and various charter agreements, we are protected from the volatility of fuel prices; however, if the
unavailability of fuel caused us to cancel flights, our revenues would be reduced.&nbsp; We continue to work diligently with Continental, United and our fuel providers to ensure that fuel is available and ready for all our flights as part of our reliability and
on-time performance program.&nbsp; Under the United Express Agreement, we agreed to a fuel risk sharing program with United whereby our markup is tied to an index consisting of the gap between increases in the price of fuel and increases in United&rsquo;s passenger
revenue per available seat mile.&nbsp; As the gap between these two metrics rise, our markup could be reduced up to 4 percentage points.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Revenues generated by Aviation Services totaled $42.6 million in 2009.&nbsp; This segment includes ground handling services and aircraft cleaning services.&nbsp; Ground
handling services include baggage handling and ticket counter services for several airlines including Continental, American Airlines and Allegiant Air at locations across the United States.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Aviation Services segment also includes ExpressJet Services.&nbsp; These entities are the North American partner to three major European original equipment
manufacturers and provide composite, sheet metal, paint, interior (including seat refurbishment) and thrust reverser repairs throughout our four facilities in the United States and Mexico.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="acfleet"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Aircraft Fleet</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u>Our Fleet</u></b></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We operate a fleet of 244 aircraft, all within the ERJ Family of jets manufactured by Embraer.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA provides for the continued lease or
sublease of our 244 Embraer regional jets.&nbsp; For substantially all of 2009, 214 aircraft operated under our Amended Continental CPA and 30 aircraft flew within our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The operational capability of the ERJ-145 is 1,100 miles.&nbsp; The ERJ-145XR, with a 1,600 mile range, continues to create potential expansion opportunities for us
whether under our network or other carriers&rsquo; networks to more economically serve cities that are the right size for our aircraft.&nbsp; We are currently the only operator of the ERJ-145XR in the world.&nbsp; Each aircraft is equipped with advanced technology
and certifications that aid our operation in challenging weather conditions and flying efficiently at higher flight altitudes.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The aircraft dedicated to our mainline partners offer a seamless jet service experience to their &nbsp;&nbsp; passengers.&nbsp; The planes feature overhead baggage
compartments, under-seat baggage storage, leather seating, lavatories, in-flight meal and beverage service capabilities and jet-bridge loading in most locations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Aircraft dedicated to our Corporate Aviation (charter) division and the United Express Agreement have redesigned seats for enhanced comfort and aircraft in our Corporate
Aviation (charter) division feature complimentary XM Satellite Radio with over 100 channels of entertainment.&nbsp; During 2009, our Corporate Aviation (charter) division operated eight aircraft in a standard 41 seat configuration which provided additional space for
the customer.&nbsp; Due to demand for our 50 seat product within the United Express Agreement, we began to reconfigure all aircraft back to the standard 50 seat configuration in late 2009 and plan to complete the modifications during the first half of
2010.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During 2009, our final 50 options with Embraer for aircraft purchases within the ERJ-145 Family expired unexercised.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u>Maintenance of Our Aircraft</u></b></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We maintain our aircraft primarily using our own trained and FAA-certified personnel and facilities.&nbsp; We perform routine maintenance and inspection of our aircraft
engines and airframes at intervals required by the FAA.&nbsp; We perform line and heavy maintenance at our facilities in Cleveland, Ohio; Houston, Texas; Knoxville, Tennessee; Newark, New Jersey; Richmond, Virginia; and Shreveport, Louisiana.&nbsp; We also perform
line maintenance at our satellite maintenance stations.&nbsp; We maintain an inventory of aircraft spare parts in an effort to ensure the reliability of our operations and utilize a computerized tracking system to increase maintenance efficiency and avoid excess
inventory of spare parts.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have a power-by-the-hour agreement with Rolls Royce to maintain the engines on our aircraft through April 2015 (the &ldquo;Rolls Agreement&rdquo;).&nbsp; Under the
Rolls Agreement, we are charged a fixed rate based on flight hours incurred during a month.&nbsp; The rates are subject to annual revisions based on specific labor and materials indices.&nbsp; We also have power-by-the-hour agreements with other key vendors to cover
various high value components and systems on the aircraft, such as auxiliary power units, avionics, environmental controls, tires, wheels and brakes.&nbsp; For 2009, approximately 72% of our maintenance, materials and repairs cost consisted of power-by-the-hour
expenses.&nbsp; We believe that these agreements, coupled with our ongoing maintenance program, reduce the likelihood of unexpected maintenance expense during the aircraft lease terms and greatly mitigate accelerating maintenance costs commonly associated with aging
aircraft.</font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><a name="copetitors"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Competitors</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The airline industry is highly competitive.&nbsp; ExpressJet competes principally with other regional airlines providing long-term service to legacy carriers, aircraft
operators providing customized on-demand charter services, and companies who offer aircraft ground handling services.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We are one of several competitors in the commercial airline market.&nbsp; Our competitors include Republic Airways (&ldquo;Republic&rdquo;), Chautauqua Airlines
(&ldquo;Chautauqua&rdquo;), Mesa Airlines (&ldquo;Mesa&rdquo;), Pinnacle Airlines (&ldquo;Pinnacle&rdquo;), Trans States, Air Wisconsin, and SkyWest Airlines (including Atlantic Southeast Airlines) (&ldquo;SkyWest&rdquo;).&nbsp; We also compete with other airlines,
such as American Eagle, Comair, Compass, Mesaba and Horizon Airlines, which are wholly owned subsidiaries of major airline holding companies.&nbsp; One of the principal challenges for airlines operating regional jets under either fixed-fee or revenue-sharing
arrangements, in addition to depending on the financial health of their partners, is the ability to maintain reliable and seamless operations with a competitively low cost structure.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" color="black" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">Given the increased regulatory and media scrutiny on regional airline carriers in the aftermath of the Colgan
Q400 accident in Buffalo, New York that occurred in February 2009, we believe we are well positioned to respond to any additional regulatory requirements, compared to our competitors.&nbsp; During the third quarter of 2009, we began implementation of our Advanced
Qualification Program.&nbsp; This program complements our current Flight Operations Quality Assurance (FOQA) Program, Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) and Threat and Error Management training and helps us in our adoption of an overall Safety Management
System.&nbsp; We currently incorporate the costs associated with these programs into our financial results and do not expect large additional expenditures as we move to an overall Safety Management System.&nbsp; Our workforce is also very senior and while it causes
additional pressures on our expenses, we believe a senior workforce, in addition to managing all training for our flight crews in-house, provides us a distinct advantage for responding to any additional regulatory requirements in a cost-effective and efficient
manner.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Due to variations in terms under the agreements pursuant to which regional airlines operate, cost comparisons between regional airlines are difficult.&nbsp; However, we
believe ExpressJet is the best operator in the industry and offers to Continental and United two of the most competitively priced agreements in the industry.&nbsp; Both of our main-line partners have benefited from our continued focus on cost, reliability and
operating efficiencies associated with a single fleet type.&nbsp; Finally, our position as the launch customer for the ERJ-145 Family and the reduced aircraft rent exposure provided under the Amended Continental CPA provides us some of the most favorable fleet
financing in the industry.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Corporate Aviation (charter) division competes in varying degrees with corporate aviation departments, non-scheduled aircraft operators and scheduled air carriers
offering non-scheduled service.&nbsp; We are the largest on-demand 50-seat aircraft operator and compete primarily with operators offering fewer seats.&nbsp; We operate under a part 121 certificate (complete commercial airline operator certificate from the FAA),
which requires higher safety standards than operators flying under a part 135 certificate (private airline operator certificate from the FAA).&nbsp; Some regional airlines, such as SkyWest and Republic, offer similar products directly to customers or through
subcontract agreements with legacy carriers such as Continental or Delta. Growing awareness of our brand as a high quality product is enabling us to achieve continued market penetration.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="2" face="Arial"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Aviation Services division competes with both airlines and non-airlines for long-term contracts to provide ground handling, maintenance services and paint
services.&nbsp; Some of these entities include Aircraft Service International, Air Wisconsin, American Eagle, Delta Global Services, Pinnacle, PrimeFlight, Servisair, SkyWest and Worldwide Flight Services.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="industry"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Industry</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The United States airline industry has been very competitive since it was deregulated in 1978.&nbsp; Since then, various business models have been developed and matured
to offer commercial air service.&nbsp; These models include hub-and spoke models (dominated by mainline carriers such as Continental and United) regional feeder models in support of the hub-and-spoke model (such as ExpressJet or Skywest), and low-cost models (such as
AirTran and Southwest Airlines) that compete on price at the expense of convenience and onboard amenities.&nbsp; The regional feeder model, developed originally by props and turbo-props, has largely given way to regional jets that now provide main-line legacy
carriers the ability to connect small markets and thin time-channels in the United States, Mexico and Canada more economically than with larger aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The hub-and spoke business model, along with the regional feeder model that supports it, attempt to gain and sustain market share by:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="672">
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">unbundling products so that each customer can create a unique travel experience they value:</font></p>

</td>
</tr>

<tr>

<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Commercial airlines have faced unprecedented challenges over the last few years including volatile fuel prices and an economy in recession.&nbsp; Higher fuel costs have
resulted in upward cost pressures, lower demand and capacity reductions that can negatively affect the demand for regional aircraft capacity.&nbsp; Inversely, as fuel prices recede or the economy weakens, the economics of regional aircraft can improve as lower demand
necessitates equipment substitutions (down gauging) from higher capacity aircraft to regional jets.&nbsp; Going forward, it is difficult to predict how demand for regional aircraft may be affected by changes in the economy or fuel price environment.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="industryregulation"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Industry Regulation</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We operate under a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued by the Department of Transportation (&ldquo;DOT&rdquo;).&nbsp; This certificate may be altered,
amended, modified or suspended by the DOT if public convenience and necessity so require.&nbsp; The DOT has jurisdiction to prohibit certain unfair or anti-competitive practices, determine carrier fitness to serve and mandate certain conditions of carriage.&nbsp; The
DOT can bring proceedings for the enforcement of its regulations under applicable federal statutes, which proceedings may result in civil penalties, revocation of certificate authority or criminal sanctions.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We also operate under an air carrier operating certificate issued by the FAA which may be amended, modified, suspended or revoked if safety in air commerce or air
transportation and the public interest so require.&nbsp; The FAA regulates airlines, primarily in the areas of flight operations, maintenance, ground facilities, hazardous materials and goods handling and other technical matters.&nbsp; Under these regulations, we
have established, and the FAA has approved, proper cargo training and handling programs and maintenance program for the aircraft that ExpressJet operates, which provides for the ongoing maintenance of these aircraft, ranging from frequent routine inspections to major
overhauls.&nbsp; The FAA enforces its regulations by the imposition of civil penalties or revocation of certificate, which can result in adverse financial impact to our operations.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="2" face="Arial"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Based on conditions in the industry, or as a result of Congressional directives or statutes, the DOT and the FAA from time to time propose and adopt new regulations or
amend existing regulations, such as the new consumer rule that limits airline tarmac delays and provides other passenger protections, which may impose additional regulatory burdens and costs on us.&nbsp; The new rule, which will take effect in April<font color=
"black">2010, will levy heavy fines against an airline when they subject customers on domestic flights to a tarmac delay of three hours or more without affording them the opportunity, within that timeframe, to deplane.&nbsp;</font> Carriers will also be required to
provide adequate food and potable drinking water for passengers within two hours of the aircraft being delayed on the tarmac and to maintain operable lavatories.&nbsp; Imposition of such laws and regulations on air carriers will increase our cost of operation, and/or
limit our operating discretion as our mainline partners could more frequently cancel flights resulting in a negative impact to our block hours.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Aviation and Transportation Security Act of 2001 (the &ldquo;ATSA&rdquo;) federalized substantially all aspects of civil aviation security and created the
Transportation Security Administration (&ldquo;TSA&rdquo;) under the Department of Homeland Security.&nbsp; The implementation of the requirements of the ATSA and other security laws and regulations resulted in increased costs for airlines and passengers, as well as
delays and disruptions in air travel.&nbsp; The TSA issued regulations implementing the ATSA, including a requirement that we adopt an air carrier security program.&nbsp; Failure to comply with TSA rules or with our security program may result in the imposition of
substantial civil penalties.&nbsp; The law also requires that checked baggage be screened by explosives detection systems, which has required significant equipment acquisition by the government and the implementation of facility and baggage process changes.&nbsp;
Further implementation of the requirements of the ATSA and other security laws and regulations have resulted in increased costs for airlines and passengers, delays and disruptions to air travel and reduced demand.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">In response to the ATSA, the TSA has initiated new security measures.&nbsp; Two of the security measures that
will have an impact on air carriers are the Secure Flight program and the proposed rule for domestic and foreign FAA-certificated aircraft repair stations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Secure Flight shifts pre-departure watch list matching responsibilities from individual air carriers to TSA and has required significant changes to the
airlines&rsquo; reservation systems.&nbsp; Air carriers are now required to obtain additional passenger information, such as the passenger&rsquo;s full name and date of birth, and the printing of boarding passes must be inhibited until air carrier is notified by TSA
that the passenger has been cleared for travel.&nbsp; The TSA's goal is to vet 100 percent of all domestic commercial flights by early 2010 and 100 percent of all international commercials flights by the end of 2010.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">The proposed rule for domestic and foreign FAA-certificated aircraft repair stations will require repair
stations to adopt a security program that includes access controls for facilities as well as aircraft and components, and restrict access by unauthorized individuals.&nbsp; The implementation of the requirements of this rule will result in increased costs for repair
stations and airlines.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">In the maintenance of our aircraft and ground equipment, we handle and use many materials that are classified as hazardous
materials&nbsp;which have the potential to generate hazardous and non-hazardous waste.&nbsp; The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and similar local agencies have jurisdiction over the handling and processing and disposal of these materials.&nbsp; We are
currently monitoring and evaluating the&nbsp;recently released Airline Drinking Water Rule (ADWR) mandated by the EPA and Federal Drug Administration (FDA) which requires airlines to develop and implement a fleet specific aircraft water system sanitization, testing
and sampling program as required&nbsp;under the new rule.&nbsp; We are also subject to the oversight of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration concerning employee safety and health matters.&nbsp; We are subject to the Federal Communications
Commission&rsquo;s jurisdiction regarding the use of radio frequencies. Federal law establishes maximum aircraft noise and emissions limits.&nbsp; All of our aircraft comply with currently applicable federal noise and emissions regulations.&nbsp; Federal law
generally preempts airports from imposing unreasonable local noise rules that restrict air carrier operations.&nbsp; However, under certain circumstances, airport operators may implement reasonable and nondiscriminatory local noise abatement procedures, which could
impact our ability to serve certain airports, particularly in off-peak hours.</font></p>

<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other regulatory actions that may be taken in the future by the U.S. government to address climate change or limit the emission of greenhouse gases by the
aviation sector are unknown at this time.&nbsp; Concerns about climate change and greenhouse gas emissions, in particular, may result in the imposition of additional legislation or regulation.&nbsp; Such legislative or regulatory action by the U.S., state or foreign
governments currently or in the future may adversely affect our business and financial results.&nbsp;&nbsp;Refer to Item 1A, <i>Risk Factors,</i> for discussion of our risks related to these regulatory actions.</font></p>

<p><a name="employees"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Employees</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our past and continuing success depends on the ability of our employees to execute effectively on a daily basis. As of December 31, 2009, we had over 5,600 employees,
comprised of approximately 2,100 pilots and instructor pilots, 1,000 flight attendants, 600 customer service personnel, 900 mechanics, 100 dispatchers and 900 supervisors, management and support personnel.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Labor costs are a significant component of airline expenses and can substantially impact our results.&nbsp; While there can be no assurance that our generally good labor
relations and high labor productivity will continue, a crucial component of our business strategy is the preservation of good relations with our employees, approximately 73% of whom are represented by unions.</font></p>

<p><a name="item1a"></a><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Item 1A.&nbsp; Risk Factors</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our business, results of operations and financial condition may encounter risks in addition to those described in this report.&nbsp; Additional risks and uncertainties
not currently known to us, or that we currently deem to be immaterial, may also adversely impair or offset our business, results of operation and financial condition.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></b> <b><i><u><font size="2">Our operations under the Amended Continental CPA may not be profitable considering impact of low escalation adjustment to
the fixed block hour rates compared to living adjustments for our labor work groups.</font></u></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We amended and restated the Original Continental CPA on June 5, 2008, which became the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; The amendment became effective on July 1, 2008. In
contrast to the Original Continental CPA in effect before the amendments, which had provided for us to earn a 10% margin on our expenses incurred flying as a regional carrier for Continental; the Amended Continental CPA now has fixed block hour rates, which are
subject to an annual adjustment tied to a consumer price index (capped at 3.5% per annum).&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, there is no downward limit for the annual adjustment therefore, in prolonged deflationary periods, the annual adjustment can be a
negative percentage. The rates under the Amended Continental CPA are considerably lower than the pre-amendment rates and will result in lower overall revenues.&nbsp; At this time, it is difficult to quantify the overall financial impact of the changes because the
pre- and post-amendment agreements are substantially different, including with respect to the services covered.&nbsp; Our results will depend, in part, on the utilization of our aircraft and the successful reduction of operating costs.&nbsp; We originally derived
significant amounts of revenue from the reimbursement, plus the 10% margin, for aircraft rent, fuel and other expenses.&nbsp; Those expenses, and the corresponding revenue, will no longer be reflected on our financial statements as they will be incurred directly by
Continental.&nbsp; Moreover, the rates we earn will be fixed, except for certain costs that will continue to be trued-up with no margins, such as property taxes, sales and use taxes and landing fees and not tied to our expenses; consequently, we could be unprofitable
if we do not manage our costs effectively.&nbsp; We would need to aggressively reduce managed expenses under the agreement if aircraft are removed from service and returned to Continental.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>We remain dependent on Continental for the majority of our revenue and cash flows.</u></font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For substantially all of 2009, we operated approximately 88% of our fleet under the Amended Continental CPA and continue to rely heavily on the financial and operational
stability of Continental.&nbsp; The domestic airline environment in the United States continues to be extremely challenging for all carriers and Continental experienced a loss for the full year of 2009.&nbsp; Continental has indicated that its own business and
financial results are subject to a number of risk factors, many of which are uncontrollable, including the amount of debt it carries, volatile fuel prices, delays in scheduled aircraft deliveries, its high labor and pension costs, service interruptions at one of its
hub airports, disruptions to the operations of any of its regional operators, disruptions in its computer systems, and industry conditions, including the airline pricing environment, an economic downturn in the U.S. and global economies, industry capacity decisions,
industry consolidation, terrorist attacks, regulatory matters, excessive taxation, the availability and cost of insurance, public health threats and the seasonal nature of the airline business.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We cannot predict the future impact of these factors on Continental.&nbsp; Moreover, changes in fare structures (most importantly in relation to business fares), booking
patterns, low-cost competitor growth, customers&rsquo; direct booking on the internet, volatile fuel prices, competitors emerging from bankruptcies with reduced cost structures, rumored industry consolidation and other changes in the industry cannot be predicted at
this time, but could have a material adverse effect on both Continental&rsquo;s and our financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.</font></p>

<p><i><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></i></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>We could lose access to our aircraft, facilities and regulatory authorizations if the Amended Continental CPA were terminated.</u></font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We currently lease or sublease all of our aircraft from Continental.&nbsp; If Continental terminated the Amended Continental CPA for cause, it would have the right to
terminate our leases and subleases for aircraft operated for Continental under the agreement at the time of termination.&nbsp; Additionally, if Continental&rsquo;s financial condition deteriorated and it filed for bankruptcy protection, it would have the ability to
reject the leases or subleases on our aircraft.&nbsp; There can be no assurance that Continental will have sufficient liquidity to fund its future operations and other financial obligations, especially in the event additional adverse factors beyond its control occur,
such as declining passenger revenue mix from global economic recessions, volatile fuel prices, terrorist attacks or adverse regulatory rulings.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Additionally, if the Amended Continental CPA were terminated for any reason, including termination at the end of its term on June 30, 2015, we could lose access to some
or substantially all of our airport facilities and other services that Continental currently provides to us, as well as our take-off and landing slots and route authorities.&nbsp; Continental leases most of the airport facilities that we use.&nbsp; We could be
required to vacate the terminal facilities (or all facilities if the termination resulted from our material breach of the Amended Continental CPA) that are subleased to us by Continental, and to use commercially reasonable efforts to assign to Continental or its
designee any lease in our name where we fly for Continental.&nbsp; Consequently, to offer commercial airline services in the same markets, we would have to arrange to use the same or other airport facilities, take-off or landing slots, route authorities and other
regulatory authorizations used for scheduled flights at potentially higher rates.&nbsp; In such event, we might not be able to gain appropriate access to airport facilities, slots or other authorizations at economically viable prices or at all.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>We may be responsible for additional taxes as a result of our tax agreement with Continental.</u></font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Holdings has a tax agreement with Continental that provides, among other things, for payments to Continental of all or a significant portion of the tax benefits realized
as a result of an internal reorganization done prior to Holdings initial public offering in 2002.&nbsp; Since that time, Holdings has made net payments of approximately $122.5 million to Continental under the agreement and could pay Continental additional amounts
through 2017.&nbsp; Payments would be conditional on achieving taxable income and the ability to utilize tax benefits as allowed.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Refer to Note 8, &ldquo;Income Taxes,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> for further discussion of income taxes, including the tax agreement
with Continental.&nbsp; If it were determined, as a result of an income tax audit or examination, that a significant amount of these tax benefits should not have been available, thus requiring us to pay additional taxes, interest and penalties to one or more tax
authorities, and if at that time Continental were unable to indemnify Holdings for these amounts as contemplated in the tax agreement, then Holdings could be responsible for such tax payments, interest and penalties.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Exercise of the Warrant issued to United could significantly dilute our current stockholders.</u></i></b></font></p>

<p><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></i></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></b> In connection with the United Express Agreement, we entered into an agreement with United which permits United to purchase up to 2.7 million shares
of common stock with an exercise price of $0.01 per share of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp; The exercise of the rights under this agreement by United will significantly change the ownership of our current stockholders.&nbsp; In addition, the fair value of the warrant will
be reflected in our financial statements as a reduction of passenger revenues over the life of the United Express Agreement, thereby negatively impacting the expected operating results of our Contract Flying segment.</p>

unprofitable to date.&nbsp; Currently, the 38 aircraft deployed outside of the Continental Express operations and the associated risks relate to approximately 16% of our fleet; however, if the Amended Continental CPA were terminated, our fleet could be significantly
