<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Contract Flying.</i></font></b> &nbsp; The decrease in operating revenue and expenses within our Contract Flying segment is primarily due to our operating a full
year under the Amended Continental CPA in 2009 compared to only six months in 2008 offset by a 42% increase in revenues from our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Aviation Services.</i></font></b> &nbsp; In 2009, Aviation Services had a segment profit margin of 35.7%, down from 45.7% in 2008. &nbsp; The decrease is due
primarily to our transition to more competitively priced stand alone ground handling contracts and the adverse impact on operating results at Saltillo due to the recession and health concerns surrounding travel to Mexico in 2009.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Maintenance, materials and repairs</font></i></b> decreased in line with the 18.3% decline in our block hours in 2009 and the reduction in our fleet that occurred
in 2008.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Other rentals and landing fees, Aircraft rentals, Aircraft fuel and related taxes, Ground handling and Marketing and distribution</i></font></b> all decreased from
2008 due to the suspension of our Branded Flying operations and the differing treatment of these expenses under the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel and paying
aircraft rent for all flights operating as Continental Express.&nbsp; In addition, Continental is directly responsible for airport facility rentals at stations served by Continental Express and for providing marketing and distribution services related to its
operations.&nbsp; Consequently, these items are not included in our Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Please refer to the comparison of operating expenses of 2008 and 2007 below for further discussion of these charges
in 2008.</p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Outside services</font></i></b> decreased 44.7% in 2009 primarily to the elimination of certain airport service related expenses such as deicing, snow removal, and
third party contracts in 2009 as they are paid for directly by Continental under the Amended Continental CPA.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Impairment of fixed assets and goodwill and Special charges</font></i>.&nbsp;</b> In 2009, we concluded that the carrying values of certain of our long-lived
assets, primarily idle general service equipment from our Aviation Services segment were no longer recoverable.&nbsp; Consequently, we recorded impairment charges of $1.3 million to write these long-lived assets down to their estimated fair values.&nbsp; Please refer
to the comparison of operating expenses of 2008 and 2007 below for a discussion of the impairment and special charges from those years.</p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other operating expenses</font></i></b> decreased by 27.0% in 2009 as a result of the elimination of costs associated with our Branded Flying operations.&nbsp;
Many expenses such as per diem, travel and relocation, passenger services and catering declined or were eliminated in 2009 due to the suspension of Branded Flying operations.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Gain on sale of short-term investments, net</i></font></b><i>&nbsp;</i> in 2009 is a result of liquidation of a portion of our ARS portfolio for amounts in excess
of carrying values.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Impairment charge on investments</font></i></b> was $0.1 million in 2009 as compared to $21.5 million in 2008.&nbsp; An impairment of $13.7 million was recorded on
our ARS holdings in 2008 due to the uncertainty in the ARS market and our need to liquidate our investments before it recovered.&nbsp; Impairments related to our equity investments of $7.8 million were recognized during 2008.&nbsp; We review our investments in
unconsolidated affiliates for impairment whenever events or changes in business circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the investments may not be fully recoverable. Refer to Note 1, &ldquo;Adjustments and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&rdquo;
and Note 4, &ldquo;Fair Value Measurements,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> for further information on our ARS.&nbsp; Refer to Note 14, &ldquo;Investments in Other Entities,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> for
further discussion of our equity impairments.</p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gain from debt discount</font></i></b> was $27.8 million in 2008 as we determined, in accordance with the Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic, that the fair
value of the liability component of our $68.5 million 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 outstanding at September 30, 2008, to be $40.7 million.&nbsp; The difference was allocated to equity and is accounted for as a debt discount which will be amortized over
the period until the next put date in August 2011.&nbsp; The fair value adjustment was recorded as a non-recurring gain under non-operating income in 2008.</p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Settlement of fuel contracts</font></i></b> was $23.1 million in 2008 as we recorded a one time sale of our fixed forward purchase contracts for periods subsequent
to September 2, 2008.</p>

therefore, we do not allocate these costs to the individual segments identified above, but evaluate them for our consolidated operation.&nbsp; We believe that the presentation of our consolidated shared costs and transition costs is consistent with the manner in
which these expenses are reviewed by our chief operating decision makers.&nbsp; These costs are included as a part of the analysis of our operating expenses below.&nbsp; As discussed in Note 1, &ldquo;Adjustments and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&rdquo;

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Contract Flying.</i></font></b> &nbsp; The decrease in operating revenue and expenses within our Contract Flying segment is primarily due to new terms under the
Amended Continental CPA which became effective July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Prior to July 1, 2008, Airlines was entitled to receive payment for each block hour that Continental scheduled it to fly and was based on a formula designed to provide Airlines with a target operating
margin of 10%.&nbsp; The Amended agreement provides payments to us at a pre-determined rate based on block hours flown that are considerably lower than the rates under the original agreement.&nbsp; Likewise, under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly
responsible for the cost of providing fuel and paying aircraft rent for all flights operating as Continental Express; therefore, these items are not included in our Consolidated Statement of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; In addition, Delta
and ExpressJet mutually agreed in July 2008 to terminate their CPA effective September 2, 2008.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b> <b><i><font size="2">Branded Flying</font></i></b><b><i><font size="2">.</font></i></b><b><font size="2">&nbsp;</font></b> <font size="2">We began Branded
Flying on April 2, 2007 and suspended these operations September 2, 2008.&nbsp; In July 2008, we announced we would suspend flying under the ExpressJet brand and Delta Prorate agreement, effective September 2008, due to record high fuel prices that made the Branded
Flying operations impossible to sustain.&nbsp; We were not profitable in this operation in 2008 or 2007.&nbsp; Revenues from this flying were approximately 17% of our total operating revenue for 2008 and slightly less than 11% of our total operating revenue for
2007.&nbsp; Average load factor within this segment was 69.1% in 2008 versus 55.7% in 2007.&nbsp; In spite of seeing improvements in operations in 2008 over 2007, unprecedented high fuel costs continued to be the driving force in determining the profitability of
Branded Flying and as such we chose to suspend the operations.&nbsp; We recognized $18 million in revenue as a result of the suspension of operations due to adjustments to our air traffic liability, frequent flier plan and certain termination payments.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Aviation Services.</i></font></b> &nbsp; In 2008, Aviation Services had a segment profit margin of 45.7%, up from 38.0% in 2007.&nbsp; This increase is due
primarily to additional ground handling contracts secured at more favorable rates than in 2007.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Wages, salaries &amp; related costs</i></font></b> decreased 9.2% from 2007 to 2008 primarily due to head count reduction in our work force related to the
suspension of Branded Flying operations.&nbsp; Additionally certain wage concessions were agreed to in 2008 under some of Airlines&rsquo; collective bargaining agreements and bonus plans were trimmed for 2008 due to our continuing losses.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Other rentals and landing fees</i></b> decreased 19.3% from 2007 to 2008.&nbsp; Airport facilities and landing fees expense was down due to decrease in contract
flying in 2008 and changes due to the Amended Continental CPA effective July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Outside simulator rent was significantly higher in 2007 due to the start-up of the new lines of business and the need to train additional staff.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Depreciation and amortization&nbsp;</font></i></b> increased 17.0% from 2007 to 2008.&nbsp; This increase is primarily due to the full year impact of capital
additions and improvements incurred in prior years as we ramped up for new operations.&nbsp; The increase was partially offset by the reduced depreciation associated with our suspension of Branded Flying as we impaired $8 million of capital assets used to support
these operations.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Outside services</font></i></b> decreased 16.6% from 2007 to 2008 primarily due to a decrease in expenses incurred to support our diversification strategy in 2007
and a reduction of approximately 50% in Continental administrative fees earned in 2008.&nbsp; This fee was cancelled in the Amended Continental CPA.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Aircraft rentals</i></b>&nbsp; decreased 42.7% primarily due to new terms under the Amended Continental CPA which became effective July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Under the
Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for paying aircraft rent for all flights operating at Continental Express; therefore, the related aircraft rent expense is not included in our Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to
July 1, 2008.&nbsp; In addition, lease payments for aircraft operating outside the Continental Express operations are contracted at significantly lower rates than previous years.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="2" face="Arial"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Aircraft fuel and related taxes</i> </b>decreased 29.5% primarily due to new terms under the Amended Continental CPA which became effective July 1, 2008.&nbsp;
Prior to July 1, 2008, our fuel price, including related fuel taxes, was capped at 71.20 cents per gallon under the Original Continental CPA.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel for all flights
operating as Continent Express; therefore, the related fuel expense is not included in our Consolidated Statements of Operation for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Ground Handling</font></i> </b>decreased 38.7% primarily due to new terms under the Amended Continental CPA which became effective July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Under the
Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for all ground handling expenses at stations served by Continental Express.&nbsp; In addition, under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fueling
services for all flights operating as Continental Express; therefore, the related ground handling and aircraft servicing expense is not included in our Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Marketing and distribution</font></i> </b>decreased 18.2% primarily due to the suspension of flying under our ExpressJet brand and Delta Prorate effective
September 2, 2008.&nbsp; All marketing and distribution cost for aircraft operating within the Amended Continental CPA is incurred by Continental.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Impairment of fixed assets and goodwill</font></i></b>&nbsp;increased $20.8 million primarily due to a $12.8 million non-cash impairment of goodwill related to the
Amended Continental CPA, and a $8.0 million non-cash impairment to write-off certain capital assets, primarily non-moveable equipment, building and aircraft improvements.&nbsp; Similar impairment charges did not occur in 2007.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Special charges</font></i> </b>increased $22.4 million primarily due to the suspension of flying under our branded commercial passenger flight operations and our
capacity purchase and pro-rate agreements with Delta in September 2008.&nbsp; In connection with these capacity reductions and the transition of up to 39 aircraft back to Continental, we incurred special charges of $21.7 million related to aircraft, employee
reductions and certain other charges in addition to a $0.7 million non-cash charge related to previously disputed base closure costs associated with the Original Continental CPA.&nbsp; Similar impairment charges did not occur in 2007.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other operating expenses</font></i></b> decreased by 27.4% in 2008 as compared to 2007 primarily due to the suspension of operations announced July 2008 for
certain business lines.&nbsp; Employee related expenses such as per diem, travel &amp; relocation, and hotels declined in relation to the reduction in employee head count.&nbsp; Passenger services and catering related expenses declined as the suspended business
operations wound down.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Gain on sale of short-term investments, net&nbsp;</i></font></b> <i></i>in 2008 is a result of liquidation of a portion of our ARS portfolio for amounts in excess
of carrying values.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Impairment charge on investments</font></i></b> was $21.5 million for 2008 as compared to $7.0 million for 2007.&nbsp; A $13.7 million impairment was recorded on
our ARS holdings in 2008.&nbsp; The need to record an other-than-temporary decline in valuation was caused by the uncertainty in the ARS market and the fact we may need to liquidate these investments before it recovers. Impairments on our equity investments of $7.8
million and $7.0 million were recognized during 2008 and 2007, respectively.&nbsp; We review our investments in unconsolidated affiliates for impairment whenever events or changes in business circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the investments may not
be fully recoverable. Refer to Note 1, &ldquo;Adjustments and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&rdquo; and Note 4, &ldquo;Fair Value Measurements,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> for further information on our ARS.&nbsp; Refer to
Note 14, &ldquo;Investments in Other Entities,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> for further discussion of our equity impairments.</p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Extinguishment of debt</font></i></b> was $2.1 million in 2008 and $0.9 million in 2007 as accounted for under the Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic.&nbsp; The
gains were calculated based on allocations of the fair value of the consideration issued in the tender offer and other repurchases of our convertible notes between the liability and equity components as compared to book value.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gain from debt discount</font></i></b> was $27.8 million in 2008 as we determined, in accordance with the Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic, that the fair
value of the liability component of our $68.5 million 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 outstanding at September 30, 2008, to be $40.7 million.&nbsp; The difference was allocated to equity and is accounted for as a debt discount which will be amortized over
the period until the next put date in August 2011.&nbsp; The fair value adjustment was recorded as a non-recurring gain under non-operating income in 2008.</p>

<p><a name="liquidity"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Liquidity, Capital Resources and Financial Position</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Sources and Uses of Cash</u></i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007, our operations used $12.3 million, $56.1 million and $39.9 million, respectively, in cash flow.&nbsp; In addition
to our cash and cash equivalents of $81.0 million and $57.5 million at December 31, 2009 and 2008, respectively, on those same dates we also had $17.7 million and $20.5 million of restricted cash.&nbsp; Our restricted cash is comprised of collateral for our
workers&rsquo; compensation coverage, customer deposits for future charter flights, letters of credit, and holdbacks required under our credit card processing agreements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, 2008 and 2007, we spent $4.9 million, $10.3 million and $48.9 million, respectively, on capital expenditures.&nbsp; A majority of the expenditures for 2008 and
2007 were spent on flight and ground equipment to support the expansion of our operations to new lines of business and building our information technology infrastructure to support these new businesses and the increase in our flight schedules under the Amended
Continental CPA.&nbsp; Of the $10.3 million spent in 2008, approximately $1.9 million was spent on capital expenditures for our strategic business ventures which are outside of the Amended Continental CPA.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In light of the current economic recession, coupled with the Amended Continental CPA that pays us at lower block hour rates and is currently operating at record low
utilization levels, we believe strict budgeting and cash preservation are crucial to sustain our liquidity and meet our financial obligations through 2010.&nbsp; We believe that our existing liquidity, projected 2010 cash flows, including the incremental sources of
liquidity described above, if needed, will be sufficient to fund current operations and our financial obligations through the year ending December 31, 2010.&nbsp; However, as noted above, factors outside our control may dictate that we alter our current plans and
expectations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In late 2009, the federal government passed the "Worker, Homeownership, and Business Assistance Act of 2009" which allowed taxpayers to elect to carry back either their
2008 or 2009 net operating loss for a period of up to five years. Holdings elected to carry back its 2008 net operating loss and recover a portion of federal regular and alternative minimum taxes paid in prior years. As a result, Holdings filed a carry back claim in
December of 2009 with the Internal Revenue Service for $17.1 million, which refund is expected to be received in the first quarter of 2010.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We did not enter into any material long-term financing transactions in 2009.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, total debt, including current maturities, totaled $49.4
million net of a discount of $13.5 million.&nbsp; Our debt consisted of the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, the Citigroup Credit Facility and the secured debt owed under a series of secured loan agreements (the &ldquo;EDC Loans&rdquo;) with Export
Development Canada.</font></p>

semi-annually.&nbsp; Holders of this debt had the right to require that we repurchase their notes at a repurchase price equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any.&nbsp; Under the indenture governing
the convertible notes, we were able to satisfy the obligation with cash, shares of our common stock, or a combination of cash and shares.&nbsp; During 2008, we took the following actions after consulting with our independent financial advisors:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The EDC Loans consist of $10.7 million loaned to us in May 2003 and $6.6 million loaned to us in September 2003.&nbsp; The EDC Loans are secured by certain of our flight
simulators, flight data software and other equipment related to the simulators. &nbsp; We used all the proceeds from the EDC Loans to reduce the principal under a note payable to Continental.&nbsp; The amount due to EDC accrues interest at the six-month LIBOR plus
1.75% per annum.&nbsp; Each of the EDC Loans has a term of 96 months and each contains customary representations, warranties and covenants.&nbsp; Additionally, Continental is the guarantor of the EDC Loans, and a default under the guarantee would cause an
acceleration of the loan.&nbsp; In 2009, we made payments in the amount of $3.8 million on the EDC Loans, of which $3.5 million was principal.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, the balance of the EDC Loans was $5.8 million.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the
fair value of the EDC Loans was approximately $5.3 million and $7.2 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In March 2009, we entered into and drew down fully on the Citigroup Credit Facility to increase our liquidity.&nbsp; The $5 million Citigroup Credit
Facility, which has a five year term and is pre-payable at any time at our election, is secured by $10 million of our ARS holdings that were purchased from Citigroup.&nbsp; Since the credit facility is secured by a portion of our ARS holdings, we classified the
liability as current on our Consolidated Balance Sheet.&nbsp; We anticipate that the Citigroup Credit Facility will remain outstanding until we successfully monetize the ARS purchased from Citigroup.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other than our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, the EDC Loans and the Citigroup Credit Facility, we do not have any other material borrowings or available
lines of credit.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Securities Repurchase Program</u></i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In July 2005, our Board of Directors authorized the expenditure of up to $30 million to repurchase shares of our common stock.&nbsp; In February 2006, the Board
authorized the inclusion of our Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023 (now our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023), within the previously announced program.&nbsp; Our Board authorized an additional $15 million in 2008 and $10 million in 2009 to be utilized
for purchases within this program.&nbsp; Purchases have been made from time to time in the open market and in privately negotiated transactions; the timing of any repurchases under the program depends on a variety of factors, including market conditions, and may be
suspended or discontinued at any time.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we had a balance of $9.7 million remaining within the program for additional purchases.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Income Taxes</u></i></b></font></p>

<p><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></u></i></b></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Arial Unicode MS">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">The tender offer and partial redemption in August 2008 of the Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023 triggered a change
in ownership limitation under Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code (&ldquo;Section 382&rdquo;) in August 2008. Section 382 limits a taxpayer's ability to utilize certain carryover tax attributes after a substantial cumulative change in ownership. This limit is
determined, in part, by the market capitalization of the company at the time of the ownership change. The Section 382 change triggered in August 2008 resulted in a significant reduction in Holdings&rsquo; deferred tax assets. At the time Holdings became aware of the
382 change, Holdings recorded a full valuation allowance against all of its deferred tax attributes at year end 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During the first part of 2009, Holdings continued to observe a significant turnover in ownership base as well as a decline in market capitalization. During the third
quarter of 2009 Holdings became aware of a second potential Section 382 change in ownership. At that time recent market capitalization suggested the possibility for further significant limitations on Holdings&rsquo; deferred tax attributes which resulted in
Holdings&rsquo; continuing to fully value its newly recorded tax assets. At the end of 2009, Holdings recorded the impact of a second observed Section 382 change in ownership. We determined that it was more likely than not that we would not be able to realize
approximately $280 million of our gross deferred tax assets related to our federal net operating losses, intangible assets, and certain other tax assets.&nbsp; Consequently, we adjusted those assets to their net realizable values as of December 31, 2009 as reflected
in the table above.&nbsp; The offset was recorded as a reduction to the valuation allowance of our deferred tax assets and liabilities.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In late 2009, the federal government passed the "Worker, Homeownership, and Business Assistance Act of 2009" which allowed taxpayers to elect to carry back either their
2008 or 2009 net operating loss for a period of up to five years. Holdings elected to carry back its 2008 net operating loss and recover a portion of federal regular and alternative minimum taxes paid in prior years. As a result, Holdings filed a carry back claim in
December of 2009 with the Internal Revenue Service for $17.1 million which is expected to be received in the first quarter of 2010.&nbsp;</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="3" face="Arial Unicode MS"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Additionally, during 2008 we recorded $8.5 million in income tax expense to record a valuation allowance for certain deferred tax assets related to capital losses and,
international and state tax net operating losses as management concluded it was more likely than not that adequate income would not be generated to utilize these deferred tax assets based on their characterization and/or carryforward period.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We account for income taxes in accordance with the subsections of ASC Topic 740, &ldquo;Income Taxes&rdquo;.&nbsp; This guidance clarifies the accounting for uncertainty
in income taxes recognized in financial statements if a position is more likely than not of being sustained by a taxing authority.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009 there were no material unrecognized tax benefits or associated accrued interest and penalties.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>Purchase Commitments</u></font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During 2009, our remaining 50 options with Embraer for aircraft purchases within the ERJ-145 Family expired unexercised.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We also have other contractual obligations of approximately $138.6 million in 2010 under our power-by-the-hour contracts with various service providers.&nbsp; The
power-by-the-hour contracts dictate the method by which we pay a vendor based on our actual level of operations in exchange for vendor coverage on specific parts and equipment on our aircraft when those parts and equipment are in need of repair or replacement.&nbsp;
Each contract varies in term and payment procedure.&nbsp; The estimated amount of our future commitment is based on assumptions related to future level of operations and forecasted payment rates.&nbsp; Forecasted payment rates are based on actual rates as of January
1, 2009 and increased annually according to the particular inflation indices detailed in each contract.&nbsp; Contractual rate increases at actual time of occurrence may be different than the forecasted rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For the year ended December 31, 2009, we spent $4.9 million on capital expenditures.&nbsp; In 2010, we anticipate spending between $9 million and $11 million in capital
expenditures of which approximately $0.5 million relate to the rollover of existing capital projects.&nbsp; We expect to fund our future capital commitments substantially through internally generated funds.&nbsp; However, there can be no assurance that sufficient
financing will be available for all aircraft and other capital expenditures not covered by firm financing commitments.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> In the ordinary course of business, we enter into operating leases related to our aircraft, spare engines and facilities.&nbsp; In accordance with U.S.
GAAP, these arrangements are not reflected on our balance sheet; however, they are reasonably likely to have a material effect on our future financial statements and financial outlook.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We enter into these arrangements to gain access to aircraft, equipment and facilities without requiring significant capital up front.&nbsp; Since these assets are used
in connection with our consolidated operations, these assets are required to generate substantially all of our passenger revenue.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; If Continental terminated the Amended Continental CPA for cause, it would have the right to terminate our leases or subleases for aircraft operating as Continental
Express under the agreement and take possession of them.&nbsp; In addition, Continental would have the ability to reject the leases and subleases on all of our aircraft if it filed for bankruptcy protection.&nbsp; Moreover, with the reduction notice and
Continental&rsquo;s ability to terminate the Amended Continental CPA, we could lose access to some or substantially all of our airport facilities. Refer to Item 1A, <i>Risk Factors</i> for additional information related to risks and uncertainties.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Aircraft Leases.</i></b>&nbsp; The primary leases on 226 aircraft in our fleet of 244 aircraft are held by Continental and expire between 2013 and 2022.&nbsp; As
we are the sublessee for such aircraft, our ability to retain access to the aircraft could be adversely affected if Continental were to default under the terms of the primary leases.&nbsp; For a more detailed description of risks related to our aircraft leases, refer
to Item 1A, <i>Risk Factors.&nbsp;</i> The remaining 18 aircraft in our fleet are owned by Continental.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, Continental was directly responsible for the aircraft rent payments for all flights operated as Continental Express under the terms of the Amended Continental
CPA.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, our 2010 expected total minimum annual rental payments under current and future non-cancelable aircraft operating leases for aircraft operating outside of the Continental Express operations was approximately $26.8
million.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Other Leases.</i></b>&nbsp; Other leases and subleases are primarily related to ground facilities (airport and maintenance) spare engines, and a flight training
device.&nbsp; These leases have greatly varying terms, which we expect, in most cases, to be renewed or replaced.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, our expected total minimum annual, non-aircraft rental payments for 2010 under current and future non-cancelable operating
leases are approximately $9.2 million. The expected total minimum rental payments for 2010, by category, are as follows (in millions):</font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other Contingent Liabilities or Commitments</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We are a party to many contracts in which it is common for us to agree to indemnify third parties for tort liabilities that arise out of or relate to the subject matter
of the contract.&nbsp; In some cases, this indemnity extends to related liabilities arising from the negligence of the indemnified parties, but usually excludes any liabilities caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct.&nbsp; We cannot estimate the potential
amount of future payments under these indemnities until events arise that would trigger a liability under the indemnities.&nbsp; However, we expect that we would be covered by insurance for any such liabilities, subject to deductibles.</font></p>

<p><a name="item7a"></a><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Item 7A.&nbsp; Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure about Market Risk</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have been and are subject to market risks, including commodity price risk (such as, to a limited extent, aircraft fuel prices) and interest rate risk.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="aircraftfule"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Aircraft Fuel</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">Prior to July 1, 2008, Continental provided all of our aircraft fuel needs for the aircraft operating as Continental Express under the Original
Continental CPA, and we incurred fuel expense and fuel tax equal to the lower of the actual cost of the fuel and the related taxes or agreed-upon caps of 66.0 cents and 5.2 cents per gallon, respectively.&nbsp; As a result, our cost of fuel was 71.2 cents per gallon
for the six months ended June 30, 2008.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel for all flights operating as Continental Express; therefore, the related fuel expense is not included in our
Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the United Express Agreement, we agreed to a fuel risk sharing program with United whereby our markup is tied to an index consisting of the gap between increases
in the price of fuel and increases in United&rsquo;s passenger revenue per available seat mile.&nbsp; As the gap between these two metrics rises, our markup could be reduced up to 4 percentage points.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="interestrates"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Interest Rates</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">We have potential interest rate exposure under the EDC Loans which bears interest at the six-month LIBOR plus 1.75% per annum.&nbsp; We also have
potential interest rate exposure under the Citigroup Credit Facility which bears interest at the open federal rate plus a variable spread per annum.&nbsp; The interest rates applicable to these variable rate notes may rise, increasing our interest expense.&nbsp; The
impact of market risk is estimated using a hypothetical increase in interest rates by 100 basis points for our variable rate long-term debt.&nbsp; Based on this hypothetical assumption, any additional amounts incurred in interest expense for both our EDC Loans and
the Citigroup Credit Facility for all periods presented would not be material.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, we estimated the fair value of our $52.1 million and $60.8 million (carrying values)
convertible notes to be $50.3 million and $38.9 million, respectively, based upon a fair valuation model that considered quoted market prices.&nbsp; Changes in the fair market value of our fixed-rate debt could be affected by a variety of factors including general
investor behavior, industry specific risks and interest rate risks.&nbsp; Holders of this debt had the right to require that we repurchase their notes on August 1, 2008.&nbsp; On that date we satisfied $59.7 million in aggregate principal of outstanding notes that
had been validly tendered. Following the completion of the tender offer, $68.5 million aggregate principal of our Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023 remained outstanding.&nbsp; In accordance with the Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic, we calculated the
fair value of the liability component of our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 to be $40.7 million and the equity component and related debt discount to be $27.8 million.&nbsp; The $27.8 million discount is being accreted to &ldquo;Amortization of debt
discount&rdquo; in our Consolidated Statements of Operations and will continue until August 1, 2011.&nbsp; Subsequent to repurchases made in 2009, our interest expense, calculated using the effective interest method, related to the debt discount will be $7.8 million
in 2010 and $5.7 million for the seven months ending July 31, 2011. In conjunction with the amortization of debt discount, we are currently amortizing $2.0 million of capitalized fees associated with the convertible debt refinancing to interest expense until August
1, 2011.</font></p>

<p align="center"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">MANAGEMENT&rsquo;S REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING<br />
</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">The Board of Directors and Stockholders of<br />
ExpressJet Holdings, Inc.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements included in this report.&nbsp; The financial statements have been
prepared in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and reflect management&rsquo;s judgments and estimates concerning effects of events and transactions that are accounted for and disclosed.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Management is also responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules 13a -15(f) and 15d - 15(f) under
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&nbsp; The internal control over financial reporting of ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of
financial statements for external purposes in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp; The Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="624">
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">(i)&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of assets of the Company;</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">(ii)&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company
are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the Company; and</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">(iii)&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">Provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the Company&rsquo;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Management recognizes that there are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of human error
and the circumvention or overriding of internal control.&nbsp; Accordingly, even effective internal control over financial reporting can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparations and may not prevent or detect
misstatements.&nbsp; Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may
deteriorate.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the
effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2009 based on the framework in Internal Control &mdash; Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&nbsp; Based on that
evaluation, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2009 has been audited by KPMG LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm,
which also audited the financial statements of the Company for the year ended December 31, 2009, as stated in their report which is presented in this Annual Report.</font></p>

<p align="center"><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">The Board of Directors and Shareholders<br />
 ExpressJet Holdings, Inc.:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheet of ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries (the Company) as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&rsquo; equity, and
cash flows for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009. In connection with our audit of the consolidated financial statements, we also have audited financial statement schedule II &ndash; Valuation and Qualifying Accounts for 2009.&nbsp; These consolidated financial
statements and financial statement schedule are the responsibility of the Company&rsquo;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audit.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the
financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant
estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries<i></i>as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, and the results
of its operations and its cash flows for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. Also in our opinion, the related financial statement schedule, when considered in relation to the basic consolidated
financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly, in all material respects, the 2009 information set forth therein.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">As discussed in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements, effective January&nbsp;1, 2009, the Company adopted the Cash Conversion Subsections of ASC Subtopic 470-20, <i>Debt with Conversion and Other Options &ndash; Cash
Conversion</i>.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), ExpressJet Holdings, Inc.&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, based on
criteria established in <i>Internal Control&mdash;Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), and our report dated February 26, 2010 expressed an unqualified opinion on the effectiveness of the
Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">/s/ KPMG LLP<br />
 Houston, Texas<br />
 February 26, 2010</font></p>

<p align="center"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM<br />
</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">The Board of Directors and Shareholders of<br />
ExpressJet Holdings, Inc.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;) as of December 31, 2008 and 2007, and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&rsquo;
equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2008. These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&rsquo;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our
audits.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the
financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements.&nbsp; An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant
estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above, present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2008 and 2007, and the consolidated results of its operations
and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2008, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles<b>.</b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">As discussed in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements, effective January 1, 2009, the Company adopted the Cash Conversion Subsections of ASC Subtopic 470-20, <i>Debt with Conversion and Other Options &ndash; Cash
Conversion.&nbsp;</i> &nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Book Antiqua"></font></p>

<p align="center"><a name="reportacctngfirmkpmg2"></a><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">The Board of Directors and Shareholders<br />
 ExpressJet Holdings, Inc.:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We have audited ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries (the Company) internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2009, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control&mdash;Integrated Framework</i> issued by
the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) <i>.</i> The Company&rsquo;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over
financial reporting, included in the accompanying <i>Management&rsquo;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</i> on page 64<i>.</i> Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting based on
our audit.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective
internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design
and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">A company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in
accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the
transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts
and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of
the company&rsquo;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may
become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">In our opinion, ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2009, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control&mdash;Integrated
Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheet of ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries as of December 31, 2009, and the
related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&rsquo; equity, and cash flows for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, and our report dated February 26, 2010, expressed an unqualified opinion on those consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">/s/ KPMG LLP<br />
Houston, Texas<br />
 February 26, 2010</font></p>

<p align="center"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">EXPRESSJET HOLDINGS, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<br />
<a name="notestofinstatements"></a>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. (&ldquo;Holdings&rdquo;), a Delaware corporation, was incorporated in August 1996 and is engaged in the business of
transporting people.&nbsp; Our principal asset is all of the issued and outstanding shares of stock of XJT Holdings, Inc., the sole stockholder of ExpressJet Airlines, Inc. (referred to in this report as &ldquo;Airlines&rdquo; and, together with XJT Holdings, Inc.
and Holdings, as &ldquo;ExpressJet&rdquo;, &ldquo;Company&rdquo;, &ldquo;we&rdquo; or &ldquo;us&rdquo;).&nbsp; Airlines currently operates a fleet of 244 aircraft flying under contractual arrangements for network carriers and entities desiring cost-effective and
fully customizable group travel Airlines is one of the largest regional airlines in the world, based on 2009 available seat miles, fleet size and passengers transported.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, ExpressJet continued to transition its business by focusing on contractual flying arrangements.&nbsp; <font color="black">In addition, we placed emphasis on
improving our balance sheet in light of the pressures of industry-wide capacity reductions and continued difficulties in the global economy.&nbsp; These</font> efforts included the repurchase of $8.7 million of our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 in the
open market, which reduced the outstanding principal balance of our convertible notes from $60.8 million as of December 31, 2008 to $52.1 million as of December 31, 2009.&nbsp; We also repurchased 3.0 million shares of our common stock in 2009.&nbsp; In late 2009, we
began to reallocate aircraft within our fleet to immediately support existing capacity needs of United Air Lines, Inc. (&ldquo;United&rdquo;) pursuant to a capacity purchase agreement effective December 1, 2009 (the &ldquo;United Express Agreement&rdquo;).&nbsp;
Additionally, revenues increased over 40% in 2009 within our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">For substantially all of 2009, we operated 214 aircraft for Continental Airlines (&ldquo;Continental&rdquo;) as Continental Express pursuant to a
capacity purchase agreement, which was amended and effective July 1, 2008, (the &ldquo;Amended Continental CPA&rdquo;) and 30 aircraft within our Corporate Aviation (charter) division.&nbsp; In early 2010, we executed the United Express Agreement, which has a
retroactive effective date of December 1, 2009, pursuant to which we will operate 22 ERJ-145 aircraft as United Express to replace flying performed by other United Express partner carriers whose contracts have expired.&nbsp; We operated a total of six aircraft under
the United Express Agreement as of December 31, 2009 and a total of 16 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of February 15, 2010.&nbsp; The remaining six aircraft will begin operating under the United Express Agreement on March 1, 2010.&nbsp; On February
15, 2010, we entered into the First Amendment to the United Express Agreement with United, pursuant to which we will fly up to ten additional aircraft for United in the current ExpressJet livery from May 2010 through December 2010.&nbsp;&nbsp; With the addition of
this flying, we expect our 2010 fleet of 244 aircraft to be allocated as follows:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <font color="black">We also provide aviation services through our two wholly owned subsidiaries, ExpressJet Services, LLC and InTech Aerospace Services, LP
(&ldquo;InTech&rdquo;) and through our and majority owned subsidiary, Saltillo Jet Center, S. de R.L. C.V. (&ldquo;Saltillo&rdquo;).&nbsp; These services include ground-handling at airport locations across the United States, aircraft composite repair and overhaul,
and aircraft interior refurbishments (interiors and paint).&nbsp; During the first half of 2007, we rebranded InTech and Saltillo so that each does business under the &ldquo;ExpressJet Services&rdquo; trade name.&nbsp; These entities are collectively referred to
herein as &ldquo;ExpressJet Services&rdquo;.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We compete with a number of regional airlines for the service we provide to our main-line airline partners and charter customers.&nbsp; We believe that our continued
success depends on our ability to provide our partners and charter customers, outstanding operational performance and customer service at a competitive price.&nbsp; Our ability to do this depends on the commitment of and execution by our over 5,600 employees on a
daily basis.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman"></font>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b> In light of the current economic recession, coupled with lower block hour rates under the Amended Continental CPA, we believe strict budgeting and cash
preservation are crucial to sustain our liquidity and meet our financial obligations through 2010.&nbsp; We believe that our existing liquidity, projected 2010 cash flows, including the incremental sources of liquidity described above, if needed, will be sufficient
to fund current operations and our financial obligations through the year ending December 31, 2010.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 1 &ndash; Adjustments and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<p><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Adopted Accounting Policies</font></u></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">Codification</font></i></b><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">.</font></b><font size="2"
color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp; Effective July 1, 2009, the Financial Accounting Standards Board&rsquo;s (&ldquo;FASB&rdquo;) Accounting Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;) became the exclusive authoritative reference for nongovernmental generally accepted
accounting principles (&ldquo;GAAP&rdquo;) in the United States.&nbsp; The ASC became the only level of authoritative GAAP and eliminated the previous four-level hierarchy.&nbsp; Our accounting policies were not affected by the conversion to ASC.&nbsp; However,
references to specific accounting standards in the footnotes to our Consolidated Financial Statements have been changed to refer to the appropriate section of ASC.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Convertible Notes</font></i></b><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">.&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">We adopted the
Cash Conversion Subsections of ASC Subtopic 470-20, &ldquo;Debt with Conversion and Other Options - Cash Conversion&rdquo; (&ldquo;Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic&rdquo;) on January 1, 2009.&nbsp; The adoption impacted the historical accounting for our original
4.25% convertible notes due 2023 issued in 2003 (the Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023&rdquo;) which on August 2, 2008, became our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023.&nbsp; We filed a Current Report on Form 8-K on October 16, 2009 to reflect the
retrospective adoption of the new accounting guidance on the 2008, 2007 and 2006 Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">Other-Than-Temporary Impairments.</font></i></b><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">In April 2009,
the FASB issued new guidance which modifies the requirements for recognizing other-than-temporarily-impaired debt securities and the presentation of other-than-temporary impairments in the financial statements. This guidance, which affects the accounting for our
portfolio of auction rate securities (&ldquo;ARS&rdquo;), was adopted during 2009.&nbsp; Other-than-temporary impairments are now reflected in our Consolidated Statements of Operations as &ldquo;Impairment charges on investments&rdquo;.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Subsequent Events.</font></i></b><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;</font></b> <font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">In May
2009, the FASB issued guidance which establishes general standards of accounting for, and disclosure of, events that occur after the balance sheet date but before financial statements are issued.&nbsp; This guidance is contained in ASC Topic 855, Subsequent
Events&rdquo; (&ldquo;ASC Topic 855&rdquo;).&nbsp; We adopted the provisions of ASC Topic 855 during 2009.&nbsp; The adoption of these provisions did not have a material effect on our Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp; The Company has evaluated subsequent
events for potential recognition and/or disclosure through March 1, 2010, the date the Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K were issued.</font></p>

<p><b><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">Other Accounting Matter</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In the process of adjusting our tax accrual for our 2008 actual tax return filed in 2009, we identified an immaterial error related to our recording of
deferred tax assets and liabilities and related valuation allowance in 2008.&nbsp; The correction of the error resulted in a $4.8 million increase to &ldquo;Deferred Income Taxes&rdquo; and a $4.8 million increase to &ldquo;Accumulated loss&rdquo; in our Consolidated
Balance Sheet as of December 31, 2008.&nbsp; In addition, the correction of the error resulted in an increase to our income tax expense and an increase to our net loss for the three months ended December 31, 2008 of $4.8 million ($0.25 per common share) and an
increase to our income tax expense and an increase to our net loss for the year ended December 31, 2008 of $4.8 million ($0.42 per common share).&nbsp; We concluded that this item was not material to the 2008 financial statements and an amendment to the Revised 2008
10-K is not required.</font></p>

<p><b><u><font size="2" face="Arial">Significant Accounting Policies</font></u></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (a) Principles of Consolidation</font></i> &ndash;</b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and include the accounts of Holdings and its subsidiaries.&nbsp; All
material intercompany transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>(b) Use of Estimates</i> &ndash;</b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial
statements and accompanying notes.&nbsp; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(c) Cash and Cash Equivalents</i> &ndash;</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash and cash equivalents consist of cash and short-term, highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into cash and have maturities of three months or less
when purchased.&nbsp; Restricted cash is our collateral for estimated future workers&rsquo; compensation claims, letters of credit, and corporate aviation deposits.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>(d) Short-term Investments &ndash;</i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Short-term investments are comprised of ARS.&nbsp; Our ARS are reflected at fair value using a discounted cash flow model and significant unobservable inputs.&nbsp; As
of December 31, 2009 we estimated the fair value of our ARS to be $9.1 million.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font></i></b>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></b></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (e) Accounts Receivables, net &ndash;</font></i></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Accounts receivable are stated at the historical carrying amount net of write-offs and allowance for uncollectible accounts.&nbsp; Our allowance for uncollectible
accounts is determined using a specific identification approach and totaled $1.5 million and $0.7 million at the end of 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(f) Spare Parts and Supplies, net &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Inventories, expendable parts and supplies relating to flight equipment are carried at average acquisition cost and are expensed when used.&nbsp; An
allowance for obsolescence is provided over the remaining estimated useful life of the related aircraft, plus allowances for spare parts currently identified as excess to reduce the carrying costs to the lower of amortized cost or net realizable value.&nbsp; These
allowances are based on our estimates, which are subject to change.&nbsp; Our allowance for obsolescence as of December 31, 2009 and 2008 was $14.4 million and $12.9 million, respectively.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(g) Property and Equipment &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Property and equipment are recorded at cost and are depreciated to estimated residual values over their estimated useful lives using the straight-line
method.&nbsp; Property and equipment acquired under capital leases are recorded at the lower of the present value of the future minimum lease payments or the fair value of the asset at the inception of the lease.&nbsp; The estimated useful lives and residual values
for our property and equipment are as follows:</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In accordance with ASC Subtopic 360-10, &ldquo;Overall -- Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets&rdquo; (&ldquo;ASC Subtopic 360-10&rdquo;), we record impairment
losses on long&ndash;lived assets used in operations when events and circumstances indicate that the assets might be impaired and the undiscounted cash flows estimated to be generated by those assets are less than the carrying amount of those assets.&nbsp; The net
carrying value of assets not recoverable is reduced to fair value.</font></p>
