<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(h) Intangible and Other Assets &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Reorganization Value in Excess of Amounts Allocable to Identifiable Assets (&ldquo;goodwill&rdquo;) represents primarily the amount that arose from
Continental&rsquo;s emergence from bankruptcy reorganization in 1993.&nbsp; Effective January 1, 2002, we adopted and began to account for this asset in accordance with ASC Subtopic 350-20, &ldquo;Goodwill&rdquo; (&ldquo;ASC Subtopic 350-20&rdquo;), which requires
testing of goodwill and intangible assets with indefinite lives for impairment rather than amortizing them.&nbsp; Due to the restructuring of our agreement with Continental, our goodwill was determined to be fully impaired in 2008 resulting in a non-cash charge of
$12.8 million.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Airport operating rights, the rights to use certain take-off and landing slots and gates, are amortized on a straight-line basis over the life of the related airport
facility lease, which approximates 20 years, with no residual value.&nbsp; During 2008 we sold the Airport operating rights at net book value.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Because of the impairments and sales noted above, our Consolidated Balance Sheets as of December 31, 2008 and December 31, 2009 do not include intangible
assets.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Capitalized costs related to our senior convertible notes is amortized on a straight-line basis through August 2011, the first date at which we may be required to
repurchase the notes, with no residual value.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(i) Deferred Credits &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Currently, our deferred credits consist of maintenance credits related to certain long-term contracts and a facility rent credit for improvements related to our
headquarters building.&nbsp; The deferred maintenance credits are amortized against maintenance, materials and repairs while our deferred rent credit is amortized against other rentals and landing fees.&nbsp; Prepayments and other current assets or current accrued
liabilities are reduced as the credits are used.&nbsp; Prior to 2009, our deferred credits included spare part and flight training credits primarily derived from our purchase agreement with Embraer.&nbsp; All spare part credits were used to offset the purchase price
of initial spare parts provisioning for our aircraft.&nbsp; Similarly, the flight training credits were used to pay for the initial simulator rent costs for our pilots.&nbsp; These deferred credits are amortized as a reduction to our aircraft rent expense over the
life of the associated aircraft lease.&nbsp; Due to the transition of our business model in 2008, we accelerated the amortization of $7.9 million in deferred credits related to spare parts and flight training.&nbsp; Deferred credit amortization totaled $0.4 million,
$0.8 million and $1.2 million for 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&nbsp; The unamortized deferred credit balances remaining as of December 31, 2009 total $0.7 million.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (j) Operating Revenue &ndash;</font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Passenger Revenue.&nbsp;</font></i></b> Our Corporate Aviation customers typically prepay flights based on estimated charges to be incurred.&nbsp; Such prepayments
are held in escrow and recorded as restricted cash and deferred revenue until the flights have operated.&nbsp; At that time we recognize the associated revenue and release the funds from escrow.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Ground Handling and Other</font></i></b>.&nbsp; We recognize our non-passenger revenue, ground handling and other revenues as services are provided.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (k) Segment Reporting</font></i> &ndash;</b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> ASC Topic 280 &ldquo;Segment Reporting&rdquo; (&ldquo;ASC Topic 280&rdquo;) requires disclosures related to components of a company for which separate
financial information is available if that segregated information is evaluated regularly by the company&rsquo;s chief operating decision makers in deciding the allocation of resources and assessing performance.&nbsp; For 2009, ExpressJet had two reportable
segments:&nbsp; Contract Flying and Aviation Services.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>(l) Wages, Salaries and Related Expenses &ndash;</i></b></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> As our collective bargaining agreements become amendable, we accrue for anticipated retroactive pay that we estimate will be due under the new
contract.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have three stock-based compensation plans:&nbsp; the ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. 2002 and 2007 Stock Incentive Plans and the ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. 2003 Employee
Stock Purchase Plan.&nbsp; The Company accounts for stock-based compensation utilizing the fair value recognition provisions of ASC Topic 718 &ldquo;Compensation &ndash; Stock Compensation&rdquo; (ASC Topic 718&rdquo;).&nbsp; Refer to Note&nbsp;12, &ldquo;Stock-Based
Compensations Plans,&rdquo; for further details.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> We are currently self-insured for a portion of our healthcare costs and have a large deductible for our workers compensation liability.&nbsp; Consequently,
reserves for the cost of claims that have not been paid or benefit costs that have been incurred but not yet reported (&ldquo;IBNR&rdquo;) as of a given date are estimated.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (m) Aircraft &amp; Facilities Leases &ndash;</font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; All of our aircraft are either leased or sub-leased from Continental.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA changed the way we pay rent for aircraft from our original
capacity purchase agreement with Continental (the &ldquo;Original Continental CPA&rdquo;).&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of paying aircraft rent for all flights operating as Continental Express.&nbsp; Lease
payments relating to the aircraft removed from the Amended Continental CPA are at reduced rental rates. Rental payments for each aircraft are fixed upon lease execution with no escalation clauses.&nbsp; We also have airport and maintenance facility leases that are
leased from airport authorities or other municipal authorities.&nbsp; In order to determine the proper classification of a lease as either an operating lease or a capital lease, we must make certain estimates at the inception of the lease relating to the economic
useful life and the fair value of an asset, as well as select an appropriate discount rate to be used in discounting future lease payments.&nbsp; The assumptions used in our lease classification analyses are based on our interpretation of available market data and
specific contract terms.&nbsp; Refer to Note 6, &ldquo;Leases,&rdquo; for further information related to our rental obligations.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (n) Maintenance and Repair Costs &ndash;</font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Maintenance and repair costs for owned and leased flight equipment, including the overhaul of aircraft components, are charged to operating expense as
incurred, except for those maintenance costs covered by power-by-the-hour agreements, which are expensed based on contractual terms.&nbsp; In 2009 and 2008, power-by-the-hour arrangements represented approximately 72% and 71%, respectively, of our maintenance,
materials and repairs costs.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(o) Income Taxes &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></i></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> Deferred income taxes, which are provided under the liability method, are determined based on differences between the financial reporting and income tax
basis of assets and liabilities and are measured using enacted tax rates and laws.&nbsp; Operating losses which are dependent on the generation of future taxable income are recorded as a deferred tax asset.&nbsp; A valuation allowance is provided on deferred tax
assets if, based on available evidence, it is more likely than not that future tax benefits will not be realized.&nbsp; The current income tax receivable represents the amount which was carried back and applied against previous years&rsquo; income.&nbsp; Refer to
Note 8, &ldquo;Income Taxes,&rdquo; for further discussion of income taxes, including the tax agreement with Continental.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(p) Fair Value Measurements &ndash;</i></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>ASC Topic 820, &ldquo;Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures<b>&rdquo;</b> (&ldquo;ASC Topic 820&rdquo;)</i> provides a consistent definition of fair value which
focuses on exit price and prioritizes, within a measurement of fair value, the use of market-based inputs over entity-specific inputs.&nbsp; The standard also establishes a three-level hierarchy for fair value measurements based on the transparency of inputs to the
valuation of an asset or liability as of the measurement date.&nbsp; The three tiers of fair value input are defined below:</font></p>

</td>

indirectly, for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities; and</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (q) Financial Instruments and Risk Management &ndash;</font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Financial Instruments.</i></b>&nbsp; Our financial instruments consist of cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, accounts receivable, accounts payable,
the secured debt owed under a series of secured loans with Export Development Canada, which loans consist of a $10.7 million loan in May 2003 and a $6.6 million loan in September 2003 (the &ldquo;EDC Loans&rdquo;), the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 and
the $5 million revolving line of credit (the &ldquo;Citigroup Credit Facility&rdquo;) with Citigroup Global Markets Inc. (&ldquo;Citigroup&rdquo;).&nbsp; The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, accounts receivable, accounts payable
and the Citigroup Credit Facility approximate fair value due to the highly liquid nature of these short-term instruments.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the fair value of the EDC Loans was approximately $5.3 million (carrying value of $ 5.8 million) and $7.2
million (carrying value of $9.3), respectively.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009 and December 31, 2008, we estimated the fair value of our $52.1 million and $60.8 million (carrying value) fixed-rate debt to be $50.3 million and $38.9 million, respectively, based upon
quoted market prices.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Credit Risk Due to Certain Concentrations.</i></b>&nbsp; We provide Continental the majority of its regional jet capacity at its hub airports, as well as
additional non&ndash;hub service.&nbsp; We are economically dependent upon Continental as most of our revenue and cash flows are received from Continental.&nbsp; If Continental defaults on the payment obligations it has to us under the Amended Continental CPA or
other agreements, then in addition to any other remedies we may have, we can offset the amount of the defaulted payments against the amounts we owe to Continental under any agreements in an amount corresponding to its defaulted payments.</font></p>

additional paid-in capital, and share amounts due to the reverse split (the &ldquo;Reverse Split&rdquo;) of our common stock in October 2008.</font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 2 &ndash; Contract Flying</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we averaged over 1,045 daily flights in our Contract Flying, offering scheduled passenger service to over 134 scheduled destinations in North
America, including Mexico as well as the Caribbean.&nbsp; We generated over $650 million of revenue (approximately 95% of our total consolidated revenue) in this segment during 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>Continental Capacity Purchase and Other Agreements</i></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><u>General</u>.</b></font></i> &nbsp; A significant portion of our revenue and cash flows is attributable to the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; Under the Amended
Continental CPA, Airlines operates flights on behalf of Continental as Continental Express.&nbsp; Continental controls and is responsible for scheduling; pricing and managing seat inventories and is entitled to all revenue associated with the operation of the
aircraft.&nbsp; We also have various other agreements with Continental that govern our relationship.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, all reservation, sales, marketing and distribution costs normally associated with operating an airline are borne by
Continental.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b> <b><i><u><font size="2">2008 Amended Continental CPA</font></u></i></b><font size="2">.&nbsp; In June 2008, we reached an agreement with Continental to
amend the Original Continental CPA.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA, which became effective July 1, 2008, has a seven-year term that is scheduled to expire on June 30, 2015.&nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental compensates us at a pre-determined
rate based on block hours flown and reimburses us for various pass-through expenses including passenger liability insurance, hull insurance, war risk insurance, landing fees and substantially all regional jet engine expenses under current long-term third-party
contracts with no margin or mark-up. &nbsp; Under the Amended Continental CPA, Continental is directly responsible for the cost of providing fuel and paying aircraft rent for all flights operated as Continental Express; therefore, these items are not included in our
Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; The fixed block hour rates are considerably lower than the rates under the original agreement, though they are also subject to annual escalations tied to a consumer price index
(capped at 3.5%) at each anniversary date, July 1.&nbsp; The consumer price index escalation used for the July 1, 2009 rate adjustment was 1.94%.&nbsp; <font color="black">We will continue to focus on aggressively managing</font> costs as certain of our costs
currently have contractual escalations that are higher then the current index escalation under the Amended Continental CPA, and the economic difficulties facing the entire airline industry.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Concurrently with the execution of the Amended Continental CPA, we entered into a settlement agreement with Continental to release the parties&rsquo; claims relating to
certain identified payments under the Original Continental CPA, including disputes previously disclosed as possible matters for arbitration.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In September 2008, we agreed with Continental on the first amendment to the Amended Continental CPA in order to compensate us for our fixed costs, which cannot be
reduced as a result of the unanticipated reduction in aircraft utilization by Continental&rsquo;s scheduling. We also agreed that if Continental, beginning in year two, increases its aircraft utilization above a pre-determined threshold, then it may receive discounts
on the agreed, pre-determined block hour rates.&nbsp; <font color="black">P</font>ursuant to the first amendment to the Amended Continental CPA, we recognized an additional $4.8 million in contract revenues related to shortfalls in aircraft utilization for the year
ended December 31, 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In December 2008, we agreed with Continental on the second amendment to the Amended Continental CPA in order to clarify certain issues related to our revenue
recognition, the fuel efficiency program in place in connection with the Amended Continental CPA and depreciation related to the aircraft we operate for Continental and excess inventory related thereto.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Pursuant to the terms of the first and second amendments to the Amended Continental CPA, beginning in July 2009 and throughout the remainder of term of the Amended
Continental CPA, <font color="black">if Continental increases utilization of our aircraft above a pre-determined threshold, then Continental will be entitled to receive a discount on the agreed, pre-determined block hour rates; provided that the aggregate discount
received by Continental shall not exceed $10 million.&nbsp; For the year ended December 31, 2009, there was an increase in utilization of our aircraft above the pre-determined threshold for such period that resulted in Continental receiving a discount in the amount
of approximately $1.2 million.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In December 2009, we agreed with Continental on the third amendment to the Amended Continental CPA&nbsp;pursuant to which, among other things, we agreed to sublease
eight aircraft from Continental that were previously operated as Continental Express under the Amended Continental CPA in order to meet our aircraft requirements under the United Express Agreement.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i><u>Scope of Agreement.</u></i></font></b>&nbsp; For substantially all of 2009, the Amended Continental CPA covered 214 of Airlines&rsquo; existing fleet of 244
aircraft.&nbsp; The Amended Continental CPA provides that we will fly a minimum of 205 aircraft for Continental <font color="black">through June 30, 2009, and a minimum of 190 aircraft for the remainder of the term.&nbsp;</font> Continental does not have the ability
to terminate the agreement without cause prior to the termination date and cannot reduce the number of aircraft covered under the agreement below 190 aircraft.&nbsp; However, the Amended Continental CPA may cover less than 190 aircraft if there is an expiration of a
Covered Aircraft head lease and there are no fifty-seat replacement aircraft (among the original 274 aircraft) being stored on behalf of Continental.&nbsp; If, at any time prior to the end of the Amended Continental CPA term, Continental proposes to engage any third
party to operate one of the original 274 aircraft, we shall have the right of first opportunity to operate that aircraft.&nbsp; <font color="black">Continental retains the right to reduce the number of aircraft to a minimum of 190 aircraft at any time during the
remainder of the initial term ending on June 30, 2015.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; United Express Agreement and Other Agreements</font></i></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></b> <b><i><u><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">General.</font></u></i></b><b><i><font size="2" color="black" face=
"Arial">&nbsp;</font></i></b> <font size="2" face="Arial">United announced in November 2009 that we were awarded a multiyear arrangement to fly 22 ERJ-145 aircraft as United Express beginning May 1, 2010.&nbsp; In February 2010, ExpressJet announced the execution of
the United Express Agreement, which agreement has an effective date retroactive to December 1, 2009.&nbsp; The United Express Agreement has an initial term expiring on April 30, 2012 for 11 aircraft and on April 30, 2013 for the remaining 11 aircraft, and contains a
renewal option, at United&rsquo;s election, for additional periods up to a total term of five years.&nbsp; Under this arrangement, United must notify ExpressJet of its intention to renew each group of aircraft not less than six month&rsquo;s prior to the end of the
term for such aircraft.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />
</div>

<font size="2" face="Arial"><br clear="all" />
</font>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We operated a total of 6 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of December&nbsp;31, 2009 and a total of 16 aircraft under the United Express Agreement as of
February 15, 1010.&nbsp; The remaining 6 aircraft will begin operating under the United Express Agreement on March 1, 2010.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On February 15, 2010, we entered into the First Amendment to the United Express Agreement with United, pursuant to which we will fly up to 10 additional for United in
the current ExpressJet livery from May 2010 though December 2010.&nbsp; United will have the option to renew these supplemental aircraft for up to four additional periods of not less than thirty days per renewal period.&nbsp; Under this arrangement, United must
notify ExpressJet of its intention to renew for the initial renewal period no later than June 15, 2010 for the first six supplemental aircraft and August 15, 2010 for the remaining four additional aircraft.&nbsp; In an effort to provide United with increased
flexibility, the amendment allows United to extend the renewal deadline for each aircraft upon certain terms and conditions.&nbsp; If United elects not to extend the term of the supplemental aircraft, the ten aircraft will be removed from service, and placed into the
Corporate Aviation (charter) operation.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; All of the aircraft operated as United Express will be sourced from our Corporate Aviation (charter) division and leased as necessary from alternate sources.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Under the terms of the United Express Agreement, United will be responsible for scheduling, marketing, pricing and revenue management on the aircraft and collecting all
passenger revenues under the United.&nbsp; Airlines' operates, maintains and finances the aircraft.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We received payments under the United Express Agreement at a pre-determined rate based on block hours and departures flown and we are reimbursed us for various
pass-through expenses including passenger liability insurance, hull insurance, war risk insurance, landing fees and fuel.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The United Express Agreement also provides for incentives and penalties based upon Airlines&rsquo; performance, including on-time arrival performance and completion
percentage rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i><u>Fuel.</u>&nbsp;</i></b> Under the United Express Agreement, we agreed to a fuel risk sharing program with United whereby our markup is tied to an index
consisting of the gap between increases in the price of fuel and increases in United&rsquo;s passenger revenue per available seat mile.&nbsp; As the gap between these two metrics rise, our markup could be reduced up to 4 percentage points.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <u>Warrant.</u>&nbsp;</font></i></b> As part of the United Express Agreement, on February 17, 2010, we issued a warrant to United for the purchase of 2.7 million
shares of common stock with an exercise price of $0.01 per share of common stock.&nbsp; We did not issue this warrant for any specified consideration, but instead in connection with The United Express Agreement covering 22 ERJ-145 aircraft for United Express service
effective December 1, 2009.&nbsp; The certificate representing the warrant contains (and certificates representing the underlying shares, when issued, will contain) restrictive legends preventing sale, transfer or other disposition, unless registered under the
Securities Act or pursuant to an exemption thereunder.&nbsp; The warrant shall terminate and become void as of the earlier of (a) the time and date the warrant is fully exercised with respect to all warrant shares pursuant to the warrant and (b) 5:00 p.m., central
time, on the date of the expiration (with respect to all tranches of aircraft and including renewal terms) or earlier termination of the United Express Agreement; provided that if the United Express Agreement is terminated due to any material default or breach by
ExpressJet, the warrant shall not terminate or become void and shall continue in full force and effect until April 30, 2013.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 3 <i>&ndash;</i> Segment Reporting</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The following business discussion is based on the two reportable segments, Contract Flying and Aviation Services, as they were structured during the year ended December
31, 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">A significant portion of our operating expenses and infrastructure is integrated across segments
(e.g., non-airport facility rentals, outside services, general and administrative expenses) in order to support our entire fleet of aircraft; therefore, we do not allocate these costs to the individual segments identified above, but evaluate them for our consolidated
operation.&nbsp; The presentation of our consolidated shared costs is consistent with the manner in which these expenses are reviewed by our chief operating decision makers.&nbsp; Consequently, the tables below present (in thousands) our operating revenues, including
inter-segment revenues, and segment profit / (losses) generated per reportable segment for the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007.&nbsp; We also included our reconciliation of the consolidated operating revenue to consolidated loss before income taxes and
of our total assets as of December 31, 2009 and 2008.&nbsp; As discussed in Note 1, &ldquo;Adjustments and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i>, our Consolidated Financial Statements for each period
presented have been adjusted for the retrospective application of the <font color="black">Debt with Conversion Options Subtopic</font>, the impact of which is not allocated to a segment, but recorded at the consolidated level.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 4 &ndash; Fair Value Measurements</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">ASC Topic 820</font><font size="2" face="Arial">provides a consistent definition of fair value which focuses on exit price and
prioritizes, within a measurement of fair value, the use of market-based inputs over entity-specific inputs. The standard also establishes a three-level hierarchy for fair value measurements based on the transparency of inputs to the valuation of an asset or
liability as of the measurement date.&nbsp; The three tiers of fair value input are defined below:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="672">
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">Level 1 &ndash; inputs to the valuation methodology which are quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities;</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">Level 2 &ndash; inputs to the valuation methodology which are quoted prices in active markets for similar assets or liabilities, quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable, either directly or
indirectly, for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities; and</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">Level 3 &ndash; inputs to the valuation methodology which are unobservable and significant to the fair value measurement.</font></p>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2008, we invested approximately $65 million in ARS which are classified as available-for-sale securities and reflected at fair value.&nbsp; The fair value of our ARS
at that time was estimated using a discounted cash flow model that considered, among other items, the collateralization underlying the ARS, the creditworthiness of our counterparties, the timing of expected future cash flows, and a discount rate which accounts for
the liquidity issue associated with the current market conditions.&nbsp; These securities were also compared, where possible, to other observable market data with similar characteristics, however, due to the contraction in the credit markets and other factors, the
market for ARS is currently trading at minimal volumes and observable market data in not readily available.&nbsp; As we could not predict when the market would recover and needing to avail ourselves the flexibility to sell our ARS in the next 12 months, we evaluated
and classified, in accordance with accounting guidance our ARS as short-term investments and recognized in the first quarter of 2008 an other-than-temporary impairment of $13.7 million.&nbsp; This impairment charge was recognized as &ldquo;Impairment charges on
investments&rdquo; in our Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In April 2009, the FASB issued new guidance <font color="black">which modified the requirements for recognizing other-than-temporarily-impaired debt securities and the
presentation of other-than-temporary impairments in the financial statements. This guidance, which affects the accounting for our portfolio of ARS,</font> was adopted during 2009.&nbsp; At the end of each quarter we now reflect declines in fair value related to these
instruments in our Consolidated Statements of Operations as &ldquo;Impairment charges on investments&rdquo;.&nbsp; <font color="black">Prior to the adoption of the new guidance on other-than-temporary-impairments, we recorded changes in fair value of our ARS that we
deemed to be temporary to accumulated other comprehensive income.&nbsp; If we determined that a future decline in value was other than temporary, it was recognized as a charge to earnings as applicable. &nbsp; Under the new guidance on
other-than-temporary-impairments if the fair value of our ARS falls below our adjusted cost basis and if it is our intent to sell the ARS, then an other-than-temporary impairment has occurred and a loss should be recorded in our Consolidated Statements of
Operations.&nbsp; As it is our intent to continue exploring opportunities to monetize the ARS, future declines in fair value below our adjusted cost basis will be deemed to be other-than-temporary and an adjustment will be recorded as &ldquo;Impairment charges on
investments&rdquo; in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; As such, we recognized an impairment charge on investments of $0.1 million for declines in fair value below the adjusted cost basis of our ARS holdings during 2009.&nbsp; Recoveries in fair value
above our adjusted cost basis of $0.7 million were credited to other comprehensive income on our Consolidated Balance Sheets during 2009.&nbsp; The fair value of our $11.1 million ARS portfolio, as calculated using a discounted cash flow model and significant
unobservable inputs (Level 3), was $9.1 million as of December 31, 2009.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In July 2009, we entered into a settlement agreement related to our ARS litigation against RBC Capital Markets Corporation et al. (collectively
&ldquo;RBC&rdquo;) with respect to certain ARS (CUSIPs 36156HAG3, 679110CM6, 709163EH8, and 78442GJC1) purchased from RBC. Among other terms, the settlement agreement provided for RBC to immediately repurchase ARS&nbsp;with an aggregate par value of $18,000,000 it
sold to ExpressJet for 87.5% of par value.&nbsp; Additionally, if within twelve months of the date of the execution of the settlement agreement, any of the ARS is redeemed or refinanced by its issuer and RBC is paid a sum representing greater than 87.5% of the par
value of that ARS, we shall&nbsp;be paid&nbsp;a sum representing the difference between (1)&nbsp;87.5% of the par value of that ARS and (2) the sum actually received by RBC.&nbsp; As part of the settlement agreement, we dismissed our lawsuit against RBC and released
claims related to RBC&rsquo;s sale of the ARS to us.&nbsp; Pursuant to this settlement, we recorded an adjustment to other comprehensive income to reverse temporary impairments of $0.3 million recognized in previous periods.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we continue to earn interest at an average rate of 1.73% on our remaining ARS whose rates are reset every 7 or 28 days, depending
on the terms of the particular instrument.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><a name="ole_link4"></a><a name="ole_link5"></a><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> We continue to closely monitor the ARS market and are aggressively pursuing the monetization of the
assets at or near face value through additional market transactions.&nbsp; In September 2009, we initiated litigation against Bank of America Corporation et al. (&ldquo;BOA&rdquo;) related to ARS that BOA sold to ExpressJet in January 2008.&nbsp; During the fourth
quarter of 2009, we consummated four separate transactions pursuant to which we sold $5.0 million of ARS purchased from BOA for 90.5% of the face value of the securities, $10.0 million of ARS purchased from BOA for 90.0% of the face value of the securities and $4.95
million of ARS purchased from BOA for 93.0% of the face value of the securities.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, the aggregate par value of our remaining ARS holdings purchased from BOA was $1.1 million.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 6 &ndash;&ndash; Leases</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">Under the Amended Continental CPA, we are not responsible for paying aircraft rent to Continental on all aircraft operated
for Continental under such agreement; therefore, these items are not included in our statements of operations for periods after June 30, 2008.&nbsp; Therefore, the aircraft operating under the Amended Continental CPA are excluded from the table below as we no longer
have future minimum lease commitments related to these aircraft.&nbsp; Lease payments relating to the aircraft removed from the Amended Continental CPA are at reduced rental rates. This rate decrease is reflected in the tables below.&nbsp; Rental payments for each
aircraft are fixed upon lease execution with no escalation clauses.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We also lease or sublease, under various operating leases, ground equipment and substantially all of our ground facilities, including facilities at public airports from
Continental or the municipalities or agencies owning and controlling such airports.&nbsp; Though the duration and terms of these leases vary greatly, we expect, in most cases, leases to be renewed or replaced by new leases as required in the normal course of
business.&nbsp; Our leases do not include residual value guarantees.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We estimated fair value of our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 based on an average of market trading activity for the convertible notes
subsequent to the tender offer that was completed in August 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">Other than the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, we do not have any material long-term borrowings or available
lines of credit.&nbsp; Pursuant to the terms of the amended indenture governing the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, we granted a security interest, with a pro-rata portion, (based on the portion that the remaining notes represent of the total convertible
notes that were issued) of assets with an appraised value of approximately $173.2 million, including approximately $79.4 million in spare parts and $93.8 million of spare engines.&nbsp; We agreed that we will not as of any fiscal year end permit the aggregate
outstanding principal amount of the Notes divided by the fair market value of the pledged collateral to be greater than certain percentages.&nbsp; If such collateral ratios are greater than the applicable maximum, we will pledge additional spare parts, spare aircraft
engines and / or cash and cash equivalents.&nbsp; If such collateral ratios are less than the required percentages, we are permitted to request a release of the security interest granted under the amended indenture on excess spare parts, spare aircraft engines and /
or cash and cash equivalents.&nbsp; In December 2009, the trustee under the amended indenture granted our request to the release of the security interest on approximately $39.9 million in spare parts and $58.6 million of spare engines.&nbsp; <font color=
"black">Pursuant to the terms of the amended indenture, we are required to deliver a certificate to the trustee from a third-party appraiser dated no later than 15 business days after January 1 of each year certifying the value of the pledged collateral for the
remaining balance notes as of January 1 or such later date.&nbsp; We delivered a certificate from our independent appraiser in January 2010 indicating that the appraised value of the spare parts that remain subject to the lien and security interest following the
foregoing release is $39.5 million and the fair value of the spare engines that remain subject to the lien and security interest following the foregoing release is $35.3 million.&nbsp; Based on the principal amount of notes remaining outstanding as of December 31,
2009, the pledged collateral required under the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 is approximately $39.2 million of spare parts and $34.5 million of spare engines.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 are guaranteed by Airlines.&nbsp; Except as otherwise specified in the amended indenture governing the 11.25%
Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, there are no restrictions on Airlines&rsquo; ability to transfer funds to Holdings in the form of cash dividends, loans or advances.&nbsp; General provisions of applicable state law, however, may limit the ability of any subsidiary
to pay dividends or make distributions to its parent in certain circumstances.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have the right to redeem the notes for cash in whole at any time, or from time to time in part, for a price equal to 100% of the principal amount plus
accrued and unpaid interest, if any.&nbsp; Additionally, pursuant to the terms of the 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes, due 2023, we can elect to use shares of common stock to repurchase any 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, the number of shares will be
equal to the repurchase price divided by 97.5% of the average closing sales price of our common stock for the five consecutive trading days ending on the third business day prior to the applicable repurchase date (adjusted to take into account the occurrence of
certain events that would require adjustment of the conversion rate).&nbsp; In certain circumstances, the notes are convertible into our common stock, at a ratio of 54.9451 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which was equivalent to an
initial conversion price of approximately $18.20 per common share.&nbsp; As a result of the Reverse Split of our common shares that occurred in October 2008, the ratio is now 5.49451 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which is equivalent to
a price of approximately $182.00 per common share.&nbsp; The ratio is subject to adjustments if certain events take place, and holders may convert only if the closing sale price per common share exceeds 120% of the conversion price for at least 20 trading days in the
30 consecutive trading day period ending on the last trading day of the preceding calendar quarter.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2009, we repurchased $8.7 million par value (book value of $6.0 million) of our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 for $7.0 million, resulting in
a net realized loss of $1.0 million.&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">In 2008, we repurchased $6.5 million par value (book value of $6.4 million) of our Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023 and $7.6 million par value (book value of $4.5 million) of our
11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023 for $10.8 million resulting in a net realized gain of $0.1 million<font color="black">.&nbsp; Subsequent to these repurchases, our interest expense, calculated using the effective interest method, related to the debt discount
will be $7.8 million in 2010 and $5.7 million for the seven months ending July 31, 2011.</font></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The EDC Loans consist of $10.7 million loaned to us in May 2003 and $6.6 million loaned to us in September 2003.&nbsp; The EDC Loans are secured by certain of our flight
simulators, flight data software and other equipment related to the simulators.&nbsp; We used all the proceeds from the EDC Loans to reduce the principal under a note we had issued to Continental.&nbsp; The amount due to EDC accrues interest at the six-month LIBOR
plus 1.75% per annum.&nbsp; Each of the EDC Loans has a term of 96 months and each contains customary representations, warranties and covenants.&nbsp; Additionally, Continental is the guarantor of the EDC Loans, and a default under the guarantee would cause an
acceleration of the loan. During 2009, we made payments in the amount of $3.8 million on the EDC Loans, of which $3.5 million related to principal.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, the outstanding principal balance of the EDC Loans was $5.8 million.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">In March 2009, we entered into and drew down fully on the Citigroup Credit Facility in an effort to provide increased liquidity with
respect to our ARS.&nbsp; The Citigroup Credit Facility, which has a five year term and is pre-payable at any time at our election, is secured by $10 million of our ARS holdings that were purchased from Citigroup.&nbsp; Since the credit facility is secured by a
portion of our ARS holdings, we classified the liability as current on our Consolidated Balance Sheet.&nbsp; We anticipate that the Citigroup Credit Facility will remain outstanding until we successfully monetize the ARS purchased from Citigroup.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other than our 11.25% Convertible Secured Notes due 2023, the EDC Loans and the Citigroup Credit Facility, we do not have any other material borrowings or available
lines of credit.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Arial Unicode MS">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">The tender offer and partial redemption in August 2008 of the Original 4.25% Convertible Notes due 2023 triggered a change
in ownership limitation under Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code (&ldquo;Section 382&rdquo;) in August 2008. Section 382 limits a taxpayer's ability to utilize certain carryover tax attributes after a substantial cumulative change in ownership. This limit is
determined, in part, by the market capitalization of the company at the time of the ownership change. The Section 382 change triggered in August 2008 resulted in a significant reduction in Holdings deferred tax assets. At the time Holdings became aware of the 382
change, Holdings recorded a full valuation allowance against all of its deferred tax attributes at year end 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During the first part of 2009, Holdings continued to observe a significant turnover in its ownership base as well as a decline in market capitalization. During the third
quarter of 2009 Holdings became aware of a second potential Section 382 change in ownership. At that time recent market capitalization suggested the possibility for further significant limitations on Holdings&rsquo; deferred tax attributes which resulted in
Holdings&rsquo; continuing to record a full valuation allowance on its newly recorded tax assets. At the end of 2009, Holdings recorded the impact of a second observed Section 382 change in ownership. We determined that it was more likely than not that we would not
be able to realize approximately $280 million of our gross deferred tax assets related to our federal net operating losses, intangible assets, and certain other tax assets.&nbsp; Consequently, we adjusted those assets to their net realizable values as of December 31,
2009 as reflected in the table above.&nbsp; The offset was recorded as a reduction to the valuation allowance of our deferred tax assets and liabilities.</font></p>

<div align="center"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman"></font>
<hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="black" align="center" />

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In late 2009, the federal government passed the "Worker, Homeownership, and Business Assistance Act of 2009" which allowed taxpayers to elect to carry back either their
2008 or 2009 net operating loss for a period of up to five years. Holdings elected to carry back its 2008 net operating loss and recover a portion of federal regular and alternative minimum taxes paid in prior years. As a result, Holdings filed a carry back claim in
December of 2009 with the Internal Revenue Service for $17.1 million which is expected to be received in the first quarter of 2010.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Additionally, during 2008 we recorded $8.5 million in income tax expense to record a valuation allowance for certain deferred tax assets related to capital losses and,
international and state tax net operating losses as management concluded it was more likely than not that adequate income would not be generated to utilize these deferred tax assets based on their characterization and/or carryforward period.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In conjunction with our initial public offering in April 2002, the tax basis of our tangible and intangible assets was adjusted to fair value.&nbsp; This adjustment to
tax basis should result in additional tax deductions being available to us through 2017.&nbsp; In accordance with our tax agreement with Continental, to the extent we generate taxable income sufficient to realize the additional tax deductions and tax attributes
allocated to us, we are required to pay Continental a percentage of the amount of tax savings actually realized, excluding the effect of any loss carry back.&nbsp; We are required to pay Continental 100% of the first third of the anticipated tax benefit, 90% of the
second third and 80% of the last third.&nbsp; If the tax benefits are not realized by the 2017 tax year, we will be obligated to pay Continental 100% of any benefit realized after that date. However, the Section 382 ownership changes Holdings recorded in 2008 and
2009 have significantly limited the amount available to use in connection with the tax sharing agreement.&nbsp; Since these payments are dependent on our ability to generate sufficient taxable income to realize these deferred tax assets, they are recorded as an
obligation to Continental within the deferred tax asset accounts, and the portion we may retain in the future is offset by a valuation allowance.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; At the time of the initial public offering, the valuation allowance and the obligation to Continental offset the step-up in basis of assets in our long-term deferred tax
asset account.&nbsp; There were no payments made to Continental under the tax agreement during the year ended December 31, 2009.&nbsp; The Section 382 ownership change that occurred in August 2008 and September 2009, and any further Section 382 ownership changes,
limit and reduce our ability to realize our gross deferred tax assets.&nbsp; Federal and many state net operating loss carryovers are subject to substantial annual limitations over their remaining life, while our regular federal tax deductions for our tax amortizable
intangible assets are limited for the five year period after each ownership change.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our tax agreement increases our dependence on Continental&rsquo;s financial condition.&nbsp; If it is determined that any of the tax benefits related to the basis
increase should not have been available at the time of utilization and, as a result, we are required to pay additional taxes, interest and penalties, then we could be adversely affected if Continental were unable to indemnify us under the agreement.</font></p>

income taxes recognized in financial statements if a position is more likely than not of being sustained by a taxing authority.&nbsp; We classify interest and penalties on tax deficiencies as charges to income tax expense.&nbsp; For the year ended December 31, 2008
we recorded a net interest charge of $1.6 million to income tax expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, there were no material unrecognized tax benefits or associated accrued interest and penalties under Topic
740.&nbsp; The calendar tax years 2003 through 2007 remain subject to examination by the Internal Revenue Service.&nbsp; Also open to examination are the Company&rsquo;s state returns still within the applicable review periods.</font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 9 - Restructuring and Related Special Charges</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In accordance with ASC Subtopic 360-10 we record impairment charges on long-lived assets used in operations when events and circumstances indicate that the assets may be
impaired, the undiscounted cash flows estimated to be generated by those assets are less than the carrying amount of those assets and the net book value of the assets exceeds their estimated fair value.&nbsp; As a result of our impairment test, we concluded the
carrying values of certain of our long-lived assets, primarily idle general service equipment from our Aviation Services segment were no longer recoverable.&nbsp; Consequently, during 2009, we recorded impairment charges of $1.3 million to write these long-lived
assets down to their estimated fair values.&nbsp; Fair values were determined based on estimated future cash flows which were considered nominal.&nbsp; No portion of the impairment charge will result in future cash expenditures.&nbsp; All other long-lived assets for
our reportable segments were tested for impairment but were concluded to be recoverable.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During 2008, we entered into the Amended Continental CPA which is based on fixed block hour rates that are considerably lower than the rates under the Original
Continental CPA, which was designed to achieve an approximate 10% margin.&nbsp; Additionally, we suspended flying under our Branded Flying operations and terminated the Delta CPA and the Delta Prorate in September 2008.&nbsp; In connection with these capacity
reductions and the transition of 30 aircraft back to Continental, we incurred special charges of $22.4 million related to aircraft, employee reductions and certain other charges.&nbsp; For further details related to the special charges incurred in 2008, refer to Note
3, &ldquo;Restructuring and Related Special Charges,&rdquo; in <i>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</i> contained in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The above costs are reflected in the line &ldquo;Special charges&rdquo; on our Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></p>

circumstances indicate that an impairment loss may have been incurred on an interim basis.&nbsp; The analysis of potential impairment of goodwill requires a two-step process.&nbsp; The first step is the estimation of fair value.&nbsp; If step one indicates that
impairment potentially exists, the second step is performed to measure the amount of impairment, if any.&nbsp; Goodwill impairment exists when the estimated fair value of goodwill is less than our carrying value.</font></p>

Express; therefore, the related fuel expense is no longer included in our Consolidated Statements of Operations for periods subsequent to July 1, 2008.&nbsp; Upon the decision to suspend operations for Airlines&rsquo; Branded Flying on July 8, 2008, we sold our fixed
forward purchase contracts for periods subsequent to September 2, 2008, which resulted in a non-operating gain of approximately $23 million.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we held $1.6 million in deposits with fuel vendors for future fuel purchases for flights
performing outside of the Continental Express operations</font>.</p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 10 &ndash; Earnings / (Loss) Per Share</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We account for earnings per share in accordance with ASC Topic 260 &ldquo;Earnings Per Share&rdquo;.&nbsp; Basic earnings per share (&ldquo;Basic EPS&rdquo;) excludes
dilution and is computed by dividing net income available to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the periods presented.&nbsp; Diluted earnings per share (&ldquo;Diluted EPS&rdquo;) reflects the potential dilution
that could occur if securities or other obligations to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock or resulted in the issuance of common stock that then shared in the earnings of the Company.&nbsp; As discussed below under &ldquo;Reverse Stock
Split,&rdquo; our stock began trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opened on October 2, 2008.&nbsp; As required per the Securities and Exchange Commission (&ldquo;SEC&rdquo;) Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 4C, &ldquo;Changes in Capital Structure&rdquo;,
the computation of basic and diluted loss per share has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the reverse stock split for all periods presented in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b>Reverse Stock Split.</b>&nbsp; On October 1, 2008, at a special meeting of our stockholders, we received stockholder approval for a proposal to affect a one-for-ten
Reverse Split of our common stock, par value $0.01 per share.&nbsp; The approved proposal also reduced the number of authorized shares of the Company&rsquo;s common stock from 400,000,000 to 150,000,000.&nbsp; The Reverse Split became effective on October 2,
2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Reverse Split was part of our continuing efforts to return to trading on all New York Stock Exchange (&ldquo;NYSE&rdquo;) Group platforms.&nbsp; In addition, the
Reverse Split was a step to allow us to return to compliance with the continued listing standard of the NYSE on January 20, 2009.&nbsp; As a result of the Reverse Split, each 10 shares of our common stock was combined into and automatically became one share of our
common stock which began trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opened on October 2, 2008, with cash paid in lieu of fractional shares.&nbsp; The Reverse Split affected all shares of our common stock and stock options outstanding immediately prior to the
effective time of the Reverse Split.&nbsp; The Certificate of Amendment did not change the par value of our common stock, which remains at $0.01 per share.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Each stockholder&rsquo;s percentage ownership in the Company and proportional voting power remains unchanged after the Reverse Split except for minor
changes and adjustments resulting from fractional shares.&nbsp; The rights and privileges of stockholders were substantially unaffected by the Reverse Split.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Reverse Split which began trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opened on October 2, 2008 is currently reflected in all share information presented in
these financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 11 &ndash;&ndash; Preferred, Common and Treasury Stock</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Preferred Stock.</i></b>&nbsp; We have 10 million shares of authorized preferred stock, par value $0.1 per share.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Common Stock.</font></i></b>&nbsp; We currently have one class of common stock, par value $.01 per share, with<b></b>22.7 million shares issued and 15.6 million
shares outstanding as of December 31, 2009.&nbsp; Each share of common stock is entitled to one vote.&nbsp; Common stockholders would participate ratably in any dividends or distributions on the common stock.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Treasury Stock.</i></b>&nbsp; Since 2005, the Board has authorized up to $55 million to repurchase shares of our common stock.&nbsp; Repurchases have been made
from time to time in the open market; the timing of any share repurchases under the program depends on a variety of factors, including market conditions, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.&nbsp; We account for our common stock repurchases using the
cost method such that when shares are reissued, proceeds in excess of cost are charged to additional paid-in capital and any deficiency is charged to accumulated earnings.&nbsp; Cost is determined using a weighted average price.&nbsp; Common stock acquired through
the program is available for general corporate purposes.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, we had a balance of $9.7 million remaining within the program for additional repurchases.&nbsp; As discussed in Note 10 to our Consolidated Financial Statements, stockholders
approved to affect a Reverse Split of our common stock in 2008.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Shares forfeited under our stock based compensation plans are held as treasury stock, which can be used to issue new restricted stock and to satisfy any exercises of
stock options.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 12 &ndash;&ndash; Stock-Based Compensation Plans</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">As of December 31, 2009, we had three stock-based compensation plans: the ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. 2002 and 2007 Stock Incentive Plans (the
&ldquo;Incentive Plans&rdquo;) and the ExpressJet Holdings, Inc. 2003 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &ldquo;ESPP&rdquo;).&nbsp; These Incentive Plans provide that we may grant awards in the form of stock options or restricted stock to our non-employee directors,
our employees or employees of our subsidiaries.&nbsp; The 2007 Incentive Plan also provides that we may grant awards in the form of performance units, stock appreciation rights, or any other right, interest or option related to shares or other property, including
cash.&nbsp; The aggregate number of shares of our common stock that may be issued under the Incentive Plans may not exceed 3.2 million shares, subject to adjustments as provided in these Incentive Plans.&nbsp; We have reserved 3.2 million shares of our common stock
for issuance under this plan.&nbsp; Options granted under these Incentive Plans have been awarded with exercise prices equaling the fair market value of the stock on the date of grant, vest over a four-year period for employees or a six-month period for non-employee
directors and expire seven years after the date of grant in the case of employees and ten years after the date of grant in the case of directors.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2">No options were granted during 2009.&nbsp; The fair value of Holdings&rsquo; options granted during 2008 and 2007 was estimated at the date of

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect for the expected term of the option at the time of grant.&nbsp; The dividend yield on our

offering.&nbsp; Our methodology is consistent with prior period volatility assumptions.&nbsp; The expected life of the options is based upon our anticipated expectations of exercise behavior since no options have been exercised since our initial public offering to
provide relevant historical data.</font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">As of December 31, 2009, there was $1.6 million of total unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested share-based
compensation arrangements granted under the Plans.&nbsp; That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of 1.6 years.&nbsp; Compensation cost recognized for the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007 was $4.1 million, $5.4 million and
$5.7 million respectively.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have available to our employees, with Board of Director and stockholder approval, an employee stock purchase plan.&nbsp; Under the plan, all of our employees are
eligible to purchase shares of our common stock at 85% of the lower of the fair market value on the first or last day of the semi-annual purchase period.&nbsp; Employees may sell shares obtained under the ESPP six months after the end of the plan period in which the
shares were purchased.&nbsp; During 2008 and 2007, 59,368 and 8,349 Reverse Split adjusted shares, respectively, of our common stock were issued to our employees at prices ranging from $4.68 to $21.08 in 2008 and prices ranging from $51.26 to $60.18 in
2007.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In July 2008, the ESPP was temporarily suspended due to the depletion of shares available under that plan.&nbsp; As a result, purchases beginning with the July 1, 2008
option period were deferred until such time that additional shares could be allocated to the plan.&nbsp; The company sought and received shareholder approval for additional shares at the annual shareholders&rsquo; meeting held May 14, 2009 and the ESPP reopened to
participants effective with the July 1, 2009 Option Period.&nbsp; No shares were purchased pursuant to the plan during 2009 and share purchases for the second option period of 2009, which was from July 1<sup>st</sup> through December 31<sup>st</sup>, were made in
January 2010 at a 15% discount from market price.&nbsp; The fair value of the purchase rights under the ESPP was estimated using the Black-Scholes model with the following assumptions for 2008 and 2007, respectively:</font></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 13 &ndash;&ndash; Employee Benefit Plans</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Effective December 31, 2002, the ExpressJet Airlines, Inc. 401(k) Savings Plan (the &ldquo;401(k) Plan&rdquo;) was adopted.&nbsp; Substantially all our domestic
employees are covered by this plan.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Effective October 1, 2004 for Airlines&rsquo; mechanics, who are represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, and January 1, 2005 for all other employees,
the 401(k) Plan was amended.&nbsp; Under the amended plan, we offer the following benefits:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="672">
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">a service-based retirement match depending on the years of service from 4.0% up to 6.0% of pay per person, which vests over five years; and</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td valign="top"></td>
<td valign="top">
<p align="right"><b><font size="2" face="Arial">&bull;&nbsp;</font></b></p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p><font size="2" face="Arial">a service-based retirement contribution depending on years of service and the terms of the collective bargaining agreements, as applicable.&nbsp; Effective January 1, 2007, the retirement contribution vesting terms changed from a
five-year cliff vesting schedule to a 5-year graded vesting schedule.</font></p>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; For the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and 2007 our total expense for the defined contribution plan was $14.2 million, $19.4 million and $21.5 million,
respectively.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Effective January 1, 2009, the 401(k) Plan was amended such that certain matches have been reduced or eliminated depending on the terms of the collective bargaining unit
or work group, as applicable.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The ExpressJet Airlines, Inc. Profit Sharing Plan (the &ldquo;Profit Sharing Plan&rdquo;) was adopted effective January 1, 2002 and amended on February 17, 2005.&nbsp;
Under this plan, if Airlines achieves a 10% operating margin, the Profit Sharing Plan will pay out 5% of eligible base pay received during the year to our eligible employees, which excludes employees whose collective bargaining agreements provide otherwise and
employees who participate in our management bonus program or any other bonus program designated by the Human Resources Committee of our Board.&nbsp; Due to our consolidated net operating losses in 2008 and 2007, no profit sharing expense was recognized.&nbsp;
Effective January 1, 2009, the Profit Sharing Plan was amended to pay out 10% of pre-tax profits.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Effective January 1, 2009, we rolled out an enhanced profit sharing plan (&ldquo;Enhanced Profit Sharing Plan&rdquo;) to all eligible employees.&nbsp; The award pool
under the Enhanced Profit Sharing Plan is 50% of pre-tax net income greater than $30 million.&nbsp; The Enhanced Profit Sharing Plan is paid out before the Profit Sharing Plan.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We also provide medical bridge coverage for employees between the ages of 60 to 65, with at least 10 years of service who have retired from the Company.&nbsp; On
December 31, 2006 we adopted the recognition and disclosure provisions of ASC Subtopic 715-20, &ldquo;Defined Benefit Plans &ndash; General&rdquo; (&ldquo;ASC Subtopic 715-20&rdquo;).&nbsp; ASC Subtopic 715-20 required the recognition of the funded status (i.e., the
difference between the fair value of plan assets and projected benefit obligations) of its defined benefit plan in the December 31, 2006 statement of financial position, with a corresponding adjustment to accumulated other comprehensive income, net of tax.&nbsp; The
adjustment to accumulated other comprehensive income at adoption represents the net unrecognized actuarial gain and unrecognized prior service costs.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In 2008, the plan to provide medical bridge coverage for non-pilot employees was frozen to not allow new retirees on or after January 1, 2009.&nbsp; As a result, we
recorded a reduction in our liability and a corresponding curtailment gain of $2.0 million in 2008.&nbsp; The gain is reflected in the line item &ldquo;Wages, salaries and related costs&rdquo; in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In December 2007, President Bush signed the Fair Treatment for Experienced Pilots Act (H.R. 4343) into law.&nbsp; This law increased the mandatory retirement age of
commercial pilots from 60 to 65.&nbsp; As a result of this legislation we no longer are required to provide medical bridge coverage to our pilots between the ages of 60 to 65.&nbsp; Our liability for medical bridge coverage for employees grand-fathered into the plan
as of December 31, 2009 and 2008 was immaterial.</font></p>
