<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Note 14 &ndash;&ndash; Investments in Other Entities</font></b></p>

<p><b><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Investments in unconsolidated companies are accounted for by the equity method of accounting when we have significant influence over the operation of the companies as
prescribed by ASC Topic 323.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <font size="2" face="Arial">In January 2006, we purchased a 44% interest in Flight Services and Systems, Inc. (&ldquo;FSS&rdquo;) for $3 million.&nbsp;
At the same time, we loaned FSS $1 million which was originally classified in Other Assets, net, on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp; The note was due and payable in full on September 30, 2007, and provided that interest was due and payable quarterly on the 15th
day following the close of each calendar quarter.&nbsp; The note provided that if International Total Services, Inc. (also owned by the non-ExpressJet owners of FSS) emerged from bankruptcy and FSS could utilize its federal income tax attributes through a transaction
or series of transactions, then any unpaid balance of the note would be deemed paid in full as a contribution by us to the capital of FSS.&nbsp; The loan interest rate was equal to the lesser of 7% per annum or the three-month LIBOR plus 150 basis points.&nbsp; In
2008, we reached a tentative agreement with FSS with respect to its obligations under the note; and accordingly, we reclassified the note from &ldquo;Other Assets, net&rdquo; to &ldquo;Investments in Other Entities&rdquo; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets pending
finalization of the agreement.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2008, we evaluated and determined that the carrying value of our investment in FSS was other-than-temporarily impaired due to the uncertainty surrounding the realizability of FSS&rsquo;s tax attributes and
FSS&rsquo;s 2008 financial performance.&nbsp; As such, we recorded an impairment charge of $2.6 million in 2008.&nbsp; This impairment charge was recognized as a decrease to our investment balance and corresponding equity loss presented in the line &ldquo;Impairment
charges on investments&rdquo; in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; On October 27, 2009, we finalized an agreement with FSS pursuant to which, among other things, FSS repurchased our interest and each party granted the other a mutual release of all
present and future claims against the other.&nbsp; The purchase price received from FSS consisted of $1.0 million and a promissory note in the amount of $600,000, which note is payable in sixty equal monthly installments of principal plus interest, with the first
payment made in December 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our proportionate share of the results of operations from FSS is included in the line &ldquo;Equity investment income (loss), net&rdquo; on our Consolidated Statements
of Operations.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>Purchase Commitments.</i></b>&nbsp; During 2009, our remaining 50 options with Embraer for aircraft purchases within the ERJ-145 Family expired
unexercised.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Prior to December 2005, under our power-by-the-hour agreement with Rolls Royce Corporation (&ldquo;Rolls Royce&rdquo;), we were obligated to acquire up to three spare
engines to support our existing aircraft and the remaining eight aircraft on firm order.&nbsp; In December 2005, we negotiated the sale of eight engines to Rolls Royce and, in exchange, entered into seven new engine leases with a Rolls Royce subsidiary.&nbsp; The
engines leased have greater interchangeability than the engines sold.&nbsp; As a result, we have satisfied our engine obligations and are no longer obligated to purchase the three engines.&nbsp; These leases are classified as operating leases; hence they are not
reflected as assets and liabilities on our balance sheet.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We also have other contractual obligations of approximately $138.6 million in 2010 under our power-by-the-hour contracts with various service providers.&nbsp; The
power-by-the-hour contracts dictate the method by which we pay a vendor based on our actual level of operations in exchange for vendor coverage on specific parts and equipment on our aircraft when those parts and equipment are in need of repair or replacement.&nbsp;
Each contract varies in term and payment procedure.&nbsp; The estimated amount of our future commitment is based on assumptions related to future level of operations and forecasted payment rates.&nbsp; Our level of operations, under our agreements with Continental
and United are determined by our partners, which have exclusive scheduling authority over our fleet covered by these agreements.&nbsp; The level of operations inherent in the estimate is based on our partner&rsquo;s most recent operating plan for us, which can be
altered at their sole discretion and included operations for the 38 aircraft operating outside the Amended Continental CPA.&nbsp; Forecasted payment rates are based on actual rates as of December 31, 2009 and increased annually according to the particular inflation
indices detailed in each contract.&nbsp; Contractual rate increases at actual time of occurrence may be different than the forecasted rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <b><i>General Guarantees and Indemnifications.</i></b>&nbsp; Pursuant to our agreements with Continental and United, we indemnify our partners for certain of our actions
and it indemnifies us for some of its actions.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Additionally, we are party to many contracts, in which it is common for us to agree to indemnify third parties for tort liabilities that arise out of or relate to the
subject matter of the contract.&nbsp; In some cases, this indemnity extends to related liabilities arising from the negligence of the indemnified parties, but typically excludes liabilities caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct.&nbsp; We cannot estimate
the potential amount of future payments under these indemnities until events arise that would trigger a liability under the indemnities.&nbsp; However, we expect to be covered by insurance for a material portion of these liabilities, subject to deductibles, policy
terms and condition.</font></p>

<p><b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Employees.</font></i></b><i></i>&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, approximately 73% of our employees were covered by collective bargaining agreements.&nbsp; Our
contracts with our dispatchers and mechanics became amendable in July 2009 and August 2009, respectively.&nbsp; The contracts with our pilots and flight attendants, will be amendable in December 2010, and August 2010, respectively.&nbsp; We are currently in
negotiations with our Dispatchers and Mechanics and will begin negotiations with our Flight Attendants and Pilots in 2010.&nbsp; Our contract with our production workers does not have a term but salaries are typically renegotiated each year.&nbsp; Our other employees
are not covered by collective bargaining agreements.</p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <b><i><font size="2" face="Arial">Legal Proceedings.</font></i></b>&nbsp; <font size="2" color="black" face="Arial">In July 2009, we entered into a
settlement agreement related to our ARS litigation against RBC with respect to certain ARS purchased from RBC. Among other terms, the settlement agreement provided for RBC to immediately repurchase ARS&nbsp;with an aggregate par value of $18,000,000 it sold to
ExpressJet for 87.5% of par value.&nbsp; Additionally, if within twelve months of the date of the execution of the settlement agreement, any of the ARS is redeemed or refinanced by its issuer and RBC is paid a sum representing greater than 87.5% of the par value of
that ARS, we shall&nbsp;be paid&nbsp;a sum representing the difference between (1)&nbsp;87.5% of the par value of that ARS and (2) the sum actually received by RBC.&nbsp; As part of the settlement agreement, we dismissed our lawsuit against RBC and released claims
related to RBC&rsquo;s sale of the ARS to us.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In September 2009, we initiated litigation against BOA related to ARS that BOA sold to ExpressJet in January 2008.&nbsp; During the fourth quarter of 2009, we
consummated four separate transactions pursuant to which we sold $5.0 million of ARS purchased from BOA for 90.5% of the face value of the securities, $10.0 million of ARS purchased from BOA for 90.0% of the face value of the securities and $4.95 million of ARS
purchased from BOA for 93.0% of the face value of the securities.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2009, the aggregate par value of our remaining ARS holdings purchased from BOA was $1.1 million.</font></p>

<p><a name="item9a"></a><b><font size="2" face="Arial">Item 9A. Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i> <i>(a) Evaluation of disclosure controls and procedures</i>.&nbsp; Based on their evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the
period covered by this report, our Interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective.</p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="3" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <i><font size="2" face="Arial">(b) Changes in internal control over financial reporting.</font></i><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp; We have not
identified any material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2009.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; No changes in our internal control over financial reporting during our most recent fiscal quarter have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect,
our internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial"></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>(c)</i> <i>The Board of Directors, acting through its Audit Committee, is responsible for the oversight of our accounting policies, financial reporting and internal
control</i>.&nbsp; The Audit Committee is comprised entirely of outside directors who are independent and approves decisions regarding the appointment or removal of the Director of Internal Audit.&nbsp; It meets periodically with management, the independent auditors
and the internal auditors to ensure that they are carrying out their responsibilities.&nbsp; The Audit Committee is also responsible for performing an oversight role by reviewing the Company&rsquo;s financial reports.&nbsp; The independent auditors and the internal
auditors have full and unlimited access to the Audit Committee, with or without management, to discuss the adequacy of internal control over financial reporting, and any other matters which they believe should be brought to the attention of the Audit
Committee.</font></p>
